    #107846. Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 11

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4233 w)

    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 11

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4233 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can.
    • It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning.
    • In a recent development, gibbs is the 1.01 in fantasy points over replacement per game (+15.9) and only trails Jaxon Smith-Njigba in winning percentage on Yahoo.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this RB column, a WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

    It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available.

    1. Jahmyr Gibbs (vs. TB) - 122.5 proj. total yards.

    In a recent development, gibbs is the 1.01 in fantasy points over replacement per game (+15.9) and only trails Jaxon Smith-Njigba in winning percentage on Yahoo. Seems good.

    In a recent development, tampa Bay has been stout against the position, ranking 32nd in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields and holding recent primary rushers like Bijan Robinson (RB28), D'Andre Swift (RB50), Chuba Hubbard (RB34) and Jaylen Warren (RB23) in check. Detroit heads into the home matchup with an implied total of 25.25 points (ninth) as 7-point home favorites. It's a difficult spot, but it's getting nearly impossible to not have him as the RB1 overall every week.

    2. Emmett Johnson (vs. ARI) - 119.5 proj. total yards.

    The Chiefs seem to be planning for Kenneth Walker III (groin) to rest another week after Johnson more than held his own in last week's blowout win. The rookie, who reminds me of a Bucky Irving type on film, handled 22 carries and six receptions, leading to 32.1 half PPR points on 20.6 expected points. Those are obviously elite RB1 numbers. Kansas City simply doesn't have another RB it trusts for the moment, and the offense is firing on all cylinders against mediocre opponents.

    The Cardinals are just that. They've allowed the fifth-most rush YPG (130) and were just schooled by Blake Corum (119 total yards) last week. A huge 28.0-point team total as 15.5-point favorites (!!!!!!) awaits.

    3. Chuba Hubbard (vs. BAL) - 99.5 proj. total yards.

    (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    According to recent reports, the Ravens defense has been one of the more underwhelming units. Their secondary has been better than their run defense, to the point that even Omarion Hampton ran well up the gut against them last Monday night. It's a shorter week for Baltimore, who is now trending out of the playoff picture. We'll see how much fight it has left. The Panthers have a 23.0-point team total (12th) as near-field-goal favorites.

    Sources indicate that 4. Javonte Williams (vs. TEN) - 92.5 proj. total yards.

    Let's keep this simple: Williams is an upside RB1 whenever the Cowboys have a 31.5-point team total, as they do here.

    (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    According to recent reports, the Titans have allowed nearly 1,500 yards over their last three games, the most in a 3-game stretch in their franchise history. Trading away mega-star DT Jeffery Simmons and Pro Bowl-caliber S Amani Hooker won't help. The starting RB against Tennessee has cleared 100 total yards in four straight contests.

    Sources indicate that 5. James Cook III (vs. MIA) - 110.5 proj. total yards.

    Cook ranks as the RB6 in half PPR points per game on RB8 usage across his last four contests, averaging 23 carries (second) and 109.8 rushing yards per game. He has scored a rushing touchdown in each of his last four games (what's upcoming?), including a season-high 157 rushing yards on 18 carries in Week 10.

    According to recent reports, the Bills are expected to beat the Dolphins by 16.5 points with a bonkers 31-point team total. Miami just lost DTs Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers to injured reserve. I don't have to tell you this is a great spot.

    It has been revealed that 6. Christian McCaffrey (vs. MIN) - 87.5 proj. total yards.

    Recent findings suggest that when McCaffrey is in the United States of America this year, he averages 22.7 half PPR points (RB2) on 16.3 expected half PPR points (RB6). Turns out, Kaelon Black is a fine role player but nothing more than that to CMC. Remember to go outside in early September while the weather is nice.

    Sources indicate that anyways, this will be a great test for the 49ers as they face the Vikings in Mexico City. They've been run on at times and won't have LB Blake Cashman, but that's about as negative as I can get on what otherwise is an elite defense. They've been fifth best against fantasy RBs this year (16.7 half PPR per game), though fantasy RB1s have held the line; James Cook III (RB7), Jahmyr Gibbs (RB5) and Jonathan Taylor (RB8). We can ding CMC's projection with the Niners projected for 24.25 points versus their current 31.75 points per game, but it can only go so far. He's a mid-range RB1.

    7. Jonah Coleman (vs. LV) - 97.5 proj. total yards.

    Sources indicate that with R.J. Harvey (knee) on IR, the backfield has been down to just two. Coleman leapfrogged J.K. Dobbins over the last pair of games, finishing as the RB7 and RB9 in expected half PPR points. Dobbins won't play on passing downs, so Coleman is grabbing some receptions alongside his rushing role. He has been just fine on tape in a good situation.

    Speaking of, the Raiders are generous when it comes to fantasy points for RBs. They've allowed, oh, just 176 rushing yards per game this month. Both Seahawks RBs played well behind three backup linemen, and CMC (RB4), Braelon Allen (RB7) and Kyren Williams (RB12) were fantasy RBs this month. Denver is listed as 10-point home favorites with an implied team total of 25.25 points (eighth).

    8. Tony Pollard (at DAL) - 94.5 proj. total yards.

    Update: Tyjae Spears went to IR.

    Pollard has been the RB8, RB3 and RB1 most recently, and it's simply been because he's breaking a ton of tackles. It's hard to believe it'll be sustainable, as star LG Peter Skoronski is on injured reserve, but Pollard is also the RB10 in expected points this month, with Cam Ward taking his game up a tier. It's still a painful offense on the whole and the floor can fall out at any point. It's best to stay tethered to his RB15 on RB16 usage standing across the entire year sample. Hopefully Carnell Tate (shoulder) can return to make the offense more potent.

    (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    The Cowboys are pathetic on defense. They've removed their sitting DC from play-calling duties, while their starters have missed a ton of tackles in crucial spots. They also don't play sound against the run, which is why they've allowed the most fantasy points to RBs (27.0) and most rushing yards per game (154) this season. Last week's 44.3 eruption from Christian McCaffrey against them was the best fantasy outing of the year by any player at any position. Beyond that, opponents facing Dallas have passed at a 47% rate in neutral situations, which is the third-lowest neutral pass rate allowed in the league. Tennessee enters as 8.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 23 points (13th).

    9. Chase Brown (at WAS) - 76.5 proj. total yards.

    Recent findings suggest that the Bengals have largely abandoned the run, which arguably isn't even a bad thing for Brown. Cincy is up to 30.9 points per game because it's first in passing success rate. Brown has a better chance of lucking into touchdowns if the team passes its way down to the goal line. We saw that happen last week when each of his scores came through the air, both out of structure.

    (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    Sources indicate that aside from the scores, Brown tallied eight receptions as a check-down option with space to operate, as defenses are going to have to play softer and softer coverage against these alien WRs. Brown can be forgettable as a talent on a severely pass-heavy offense, and still finish as a low-end RB1 in fantasy due to the scoring bonanza. He's the RB1 in receptions per game (5.2).

    The next victim of the Bengals' offense will be the Commanders, who don't have two of their top DTs and were struggling through the air before anyway. The Bengals are up to a 30.5-point team total.

    In a recent development, 10. Bucky Irving (at DET) - 81.5 proj. total yards.

    This assumes Jalon Daniels is back at QB with Baker Mayfield (foot) picking up a new injury during the bye week. The Bucs are likely going to be extremely run-heavy, as they've been for the past two months with the OL smoking defenses up front. Irving has been the RB7 on RB11 usage this season, with 21.0+ half PPR points in 4 of 5 recent games. He's averaged 22.2 carries during that stretch, with games against pretty easy opponents. That's too massive to fail, especially given how slippery he is on tape.

    According to recent reports, the Lions are a pass funnel typically, but the losses of LB Jack Campbell, EDGE Aidan Hutchinson and CB D.J. Reed (questionable) make them fairly bad in both phases. They still have some DTs to worry about, but the Bucs should be able to run it here, despite the spreadsheets suggesting otherwise. Tampa Bay will attempt to bleed out the clock as 7-point road dogs with a team total of 18.25 points (21st). Irving should absorb a lot of that team total.

    11. Derrick Henry (at CAR) - 76.5 proj. total yards.

    Recent findings suggest that the Ravens are going to pass more with Jacoby Brissett at QB and with the OL struggling, especially when first-round rookie LG Vega Ioane isn't on the field. Henry can still score goal-line touchdowns as he did on Monday night, but a real reset is warranted in terms of efficiency and rushing volume if the Ravens aren't expected to be crushing teams as often as they would've with Lamar Jackson, who is hoping to return around Week 16 if things go to plan. In the meantime, it's possible Henry catches an extra target or two based on the scheme changing, but that won't even out the loss of projected touchdowns. He'll settle in as a boom-bust RB2 the rest of the way.

    According to recent reports, the Panthers have cleaned things up with better health and a upcoming DC recently, but Carolina has bled fantasy points to RBs (24.8, third) across the season. It was Jonah Coleman (RB6) two weeks ago and Josh Jacobs (RB11) and Bucky Irving (RB2) before that. A 21.0-point team total isn't the worst thing this week, with six teams on bye and five others projected for fewer than 17.0.

    Sources indicate that 12. Bhayshul Tuten (at NYG) - 88.5 proj. total yards.

    Tuten set a career high with 28.1 expected half PPR points last week, with 26 carries and three receptions. Many of those were failed goal-line attempts, but Tuten did score late en route to an RB10 on RB1 usage outing. He's now the RB10 on RB17 usage this season as a low-end RB1 with weekly upside. Chris Rodriguez Jr. will vulture the occasional touchdown, but otherwise, it's all Tuten now. The only marginal matter is that the already suspect Jaguars OL is now missing C Robert Hainsey (knee) for the next couple of weeks.

    The Giants rank 25th in half PPR points allowed to opposing RBs at 17.1 points per game. That includes ranking 23rd in points allowed on RB rushing plays (11.3 per game) and 20th on RB receiving plays (5.8 per game). Opposing lead rushers have routinely been held in check against them recently, with no RB clearly the top-24 over their past three games. DROY favorite Arvell Reese has a lot to do with that. Jacksonville heads on the road as 6-point favorites with an implied team total of 26.25 points (seventh). It's more of a mediocre matchup for Tuten.

    It has been revealed that 13. D'Andre Swift (vs. NO) - 83.5 proj. total yards.

    Kyle Monangai (toe) is back. Here are Swift's splits with him since Week 5 of last year, when the offense became the version we have today.

    (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    Sources indicate that for context, 13.9 half PPR points is the RB16 right now, while 13.0 expected points is the RB17. Those are probably closer to his per-game floor the rest of the way, but it is a real reset for Swift's baseline projection. He can still have RB1 moments with Monangai. They will just happen less often.

    In a recent development, the Saints are a great spot to sneak in a fantasy RB1 moment! They've allowed the second-most fantasy points to RBs on the sixth-most rushing yards per game (130). Chuba Hubbard ran right through tackles last week, something that's happened way too often this year. Chicago has a monster 30.0-point team total, so both backs are obvious starts.

    14. Jaylen Warren (at PHI) - 95.5 proj. total yards.

    Warren has settled in as an upside RB2 with Rico Dowdle back in the mix. He's averaged 14.0 carries and 2.8 receptions this month, leading to RB17 on RB19 usage. The Steelers haven't played great ball on offense over that stretch and just watched LG Mason McCormick dislocate his ankle last week. The OL being great this season has certainly helped Warren, who has been a top-5 RB to my eyes this year beyond that.

    (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    The matchup is reassuring. This is an eruption spot, looking at the EPA numbers on the ground. The Eagles have struggled all year, then traded away run-stuffing DT Jordan Davis at the deadline. There are fewer reasons to be afraid of what used to be an impossible opponent, and the lines reflect that. Pittsburgh enters as 4.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 21.5 points (15th).

    15. David Montgomery (vs. IND) - 67.5 proj. total yards.

    In a recent development, montgomery got in a full practice last Friday before being ruled out, but has practiced in full leading up to Thursday Night Football this week. Woody Marks (concussion) won't play, leaving Monty with Emari Demercado, who missed some lanes in the second half of last game. It won't be a surprise if the desperate Texans use Montgomery as a bell cow despite him being out since Week 5. They don't have a real choice. Of course, the Texans' bell cow RB hasn't been very valuable so far. Since Week 6, the Texans RBs are averaging 16.8 expected half PPR points per game with very mid efficiency. Montgomery finishing with 15-20 expected points shouldn't come as a surprise this week, considering the opponent.

    (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    The Colts haven't been competitive all year, especially without their best linemen on both sides of the ball. This month, Indy has allowed the sixth-most rushing yards per game (144). This season, they've allowed the sixth-most points to fantasy RBs (23.0). There really are no excuses for Houston this time around. They own a 28.5-point team total at home as 12.5-point favorites.

    16. Omarion Hampton (vs. NYJ) - 71.5 proj. total yards.

    According to recent reports, hampton set season highs in fantasy points (17.0 half PPR) and usage (15.9 expected) last week, in their first win of the year. Hampton handled 22 carries in a run-heavy game blueprint that continued because the scoreboard finally allowed for it. The Chargers are first in neutral run rate (61%), so don't be surprised if Hampton's fantasy performances tick up if they can stay more competitive after a brutal schedule. You can see the extra carries in the second half of last week here:.

    (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports).

    On tape, Hampton was used slightly differently last week. He handled nine pitches, which is the second-most by a player in a single game all year. Instead of being pointed to the perimeter, many of them got him going straight downhill, where his attributes are maximized. They also ran more man concepts instead of the wide zone stuff OC Mike McDaniel typically calls for. It's a meeting in the middle between player and coach, one that was long overdue.

    Sources indicate that this week, the Chargers are favored. I repeat, the Chargers are favored against the Jets. They don't have their best run-stopping DT right now either, which has helped opposing teams rack up 154 rushing yards per game this month (fourth). James Cook III (RB7) and Kenneth Walker III (RB1) just went nuclear against them, but even Ollie Gordon II had 103 total yards and a score in Week 7, too. This is easily the best it's looked for Hampton since the games started this year.

    Industry observers note that 17. Cam Skattebo (vs. JAX) - 72.5 proj. total yards.

    According to recent reports, skattebo is back to bell-cow work with Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR and Najee Harris released. Devin Singletary failed in that role when Skattebo missed in Week 9, then Skattebo delivered an RB5 on RB6 usage outing in Week 10 against the Commanders. They've had extended rest to get Skattebo prepared for another heavy workload in a balanced offense. It won't be surprising to see Skattebo emerge as a fantasy RB2 for the rest of the way, especially if his three grabs from Week 10 hold up.

    In a recent development, the Jaguars defense has been stingy to opposing backfields, ranking 29th in half PPR points allowed to RBs. They did concede an RB8 weekly finish to Tony Pollard in Week 10 without DT Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates active, though Jonathan Taylor managed just 4.7 points (RB37) against them in Week 8 when they did have a star run-stuffing DT. Opposing offenses have leaned heavily into the pass against Jacksonville with a 59% neutral pass rate (second highest). I doubt the Giants will do that too much given their coaches and personnel, but it's a difficult matchup regardless. Latest York enters as 6-point home underdogs with an implied team total of 20.25 points (18th).

    It has been revealed that 18. Saquon Barkley (vs. PIT) - 75.5 proj. total yards.

    Industry observers note that barkley is impossible to get a grasp on due to his injuries, the moving parts on the OL and now Joe Milton at QB. In a part-time role on a lousy offense in three games before the bye, Barkley was the RB25, RB21 and RB20 on RB26 usage. He looked good when he was on the field, and the OL did seem to be in a bit of a better spot on tape. I can see him out-kicking those marks after the bye, which hopefully has allowed him to get healthier. The Eagles' offense is in a spot where they can fully clunker at any time, so the floor doesn't exist.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.
    • According to recent reports, the report claims that "after the U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the tech giant "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    According to recent reports, the report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also noted that upcoming export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    Recent findings suggest that the allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    Sources indicate that "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson mentioned in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the firm's recent earnings call that China is an "key" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

    📅 14 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5405 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.
    • Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.
    • Sources indicate that the visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

    Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

    Sources indicate that the visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

    LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

    Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

    According to recent reports, peixoto remarked: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

    “We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

    “We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”.

    Sources indicate that tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

    Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

    In a recent development, “Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we highlighted there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”.

    The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

    However, Wolves scored the first goal of the fresh campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

    "A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

    Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

    The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

    Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

    "It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

    Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

    However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

    Wolverhampton: Bentley, Trippier, Mosquera, Toti Gomes, Wolfe, Lopez, Andre Trindade, Munetsi, Rodrigo Gomes, Armstrong, Mane.Subs used: Jiménez 60 (Mateus Mané), ‌Doyle ‌67 (Rodrigo Gomes), ⁠Tchatchoua 67 (Trippier), Pedro Lima 79 (André),Chirewa 79 (Møller Wolfe)Scorers: M. Munetsi 18, R. Jiménez 90+3penYellow card: Mateus Mané 52Blackburn: Toth, Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering, Montgomery, Forshaw, Morishita, Cantwell, Afolayan, Gudjohnsen.Subs used: Sam Morsy 55 (Forshaw), Fevrier 68 (Afolayan), Ohashi ‌68 (Cantwell), Garrett ​79 (Gudjohnsen), ⁠Yuri Ribeiro79 (Morishita)Scorers: ⁠S. McLoughlin 27, A. Gudjohnsen 48Yellow card: Pickering ​34, Cantwell 35, ‌Forshaw 45Attendance: 30,984Referee: Farai ⁠Hallam.

    “I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a massive call.”.

    In a recent development, “We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”.

    “It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is key. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”.

    According to recent reports, “Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”.

    Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc.

    “Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case. Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”.

    “Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”.

    Saturday:Bolton vs PrestonBristol City vs MillwallCharlton vs DerbyMiddlesbrough vs LincolnNorwich vs West BromPortsmouth vs QPRStoke vs SwanseaSheffield United vs Birmingham.

    Sunday:Watford vs SouthamptonBurnley vs West Ham.

    Bentley spills the corner but gets a free-kick. Moments later, the referee blows his whistle for the final time and the game ends level at 2-2. A dramatic opening night of the upcoming Championship season at Molineux. If the Championship continues in this vein all season, it will be one hell of a year.

    Blackburn nearly score a late winner as Garrett’s shot is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a later Blackburn corner.

    It has been revealed that he sends Toth the wrong way and calmly slots home to bring Wolves level in added time. That penalty decision will certainly create some debate. The Championship is always full of drama and we get some on opening night.

    LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

    It just had to be. Jimenez rescues Wolves from the penalty spot.

    Drama on the opening night of the campaign.

    Relief for Wolves, heartbreak for Blackburn.

    Industry observers note that late drama at Molineux! The cross is sent in from the left and the ball strikes the arm Alebiosu on the edge of the box. Was it inside or outside the penalty area? It is definitely handball but was it outside the box? It was very, very close but there is no VAR in the Championship so the penalty will stand.

    Four added minutes. Are we on the verge of seeing the first shock of the newly introduced Championship season on opening night?

    Four minutes added. Not even a reaction from the home crowd.

    Wolves are desperately running out of time and Blackburn still look comfortable.

    Home fans are beginning to filter out slowly.

    According to recent reports, mosquera is still struggling but he has come back on whilst limping around. I cannot imagine there will be too much in terms of added time, either three or four minutes would be my guess, no more.

    Ohashi is played in behind and goes down under a challenge from Toti on the edge of the Wolves box but those appeals are waved away.

    Recent findings suggest that mosquera has gone down again and he may not be able to continue as he receives treatment on the sidelines. Wolves may be ending this game down to 10 men.

    Industry observers note that fevrier’s shot from outside the Wolves penalty area is blocked and spins behind for a corner in front of the travelling Blackburn fans. The corner comes to nothing.

    Wolves struggling to create anything of note even with Jimenez’s introduction.

    Sources indicate that centre-back Mosquera has gone up front but appears to be struggling with an injury. He’s jogged back to his natural position now.

    According to recent reports, desperate long balls being sent forward but Blackburn look comfortable for now. The home fans are quite audibly unhappy with this second-half showing.

    Rovers fans still making the noise.

    Wolves do not currently look like scoring an equaliser.

    Industry observers note that mosquera is struggling with a knock but Wolves made all five changes. If he is unable to continue, Wolves will have to finish off with ten men.

    The frustration inside Molineux is growing and the home fans want to see some more urgency from their side as they trail with under 10 minutes left.

    Blackburn are now going to make their final two alterations of the night as Ribeiro and Garrett come on.

    Wolves are going to make their final two substitutions as Lima and Chirewa replace Moller Wolfe and Andre.

    Blackburn are looking pretty comfortable right now defending their lead and counter-attacking effectively.

    Wolves want a penalty as Armstrong goes down inside the box after making a run in behind but the appeals are waved away. Rightly so as Armstrong was not fouled.

    Wolves are pushing to find an equaliser but are struggling to carve out many genuine opportunities.

    Ohashi is penalised for a foul on F Lopez not far outside the Blackburn penalty area and that was pretty harsh on Ohashi. Jimenez is lining this one up as is F Lopez.

    The former takes but his effort hits the wall.

    Wolves’ frustration right now is summed up by a dreadful cross from F Lopez from the right side of the box that goes behind for a goal kick. The TV cameras then turn to some of the Wolves fans, who look rather forlorn in the stands.

    According to recent reports, double changes for both sides. For Wolves, Doyle and Tchatchoua come on. For Blackburn, Fevrier and Ohasi enter the fray.

    You’d have thought a goal had gone in such is the reaction from the home crowd to Jimenez’s introduction. I have to say, I’m surprised Mane has made way but Jimenez will play through the middle with Armstrong moved out to the left.

    When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager fresh to English football, it proved a vintage season.

    Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the massive question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

    Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

    It has been revealed that “I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

    Recent findings suggest that “There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”.

    According to recent reports, our experts have been having their say ahead of the upcoming Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:.

    Recent findings suggest that it is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

    According to recent reports, the 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are fresh playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

    Wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

    “I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

    According to recent reports, “It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our significant goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”.

    They have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

    Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

    “I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray stated. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”.

    These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

    Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (739 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a major win for the organization and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    Some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    Sources indicate that adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and said it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the big indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    It has been revealed that "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he said.

    Part of the challenge, Niles mentioned, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," said JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he said, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan remarked. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the company in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he stated. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    One bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    #107819. Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a big buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (410 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a big buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (410 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence tech giant in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • Industry observers note that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence tech giant in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    Industry observers note that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    In a recent development, anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    According to recent reports, "We're climbing a wall of worry," said Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, upcoming technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    The Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood said she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    In her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    Ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the massive losses.

    The fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she remarked. "That's how crazy things were.".

    #107814. As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (436 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (436 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • Recent findings suggest that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Industry observers note that as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    Recent findings suggest that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the fresh tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders substantial and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," stated Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

    The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

    During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

    Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

    Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

    Sources indicate that jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

    Recent findings suggest that newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

    After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

    In a recent development, newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

    It has been revealed that the North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

    According to recent reports, newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

    Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

    Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059.

    A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

    Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

    Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

    There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

    Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

    Chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

    In a recent development, newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

    The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

    Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

    Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

    The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

    In a recent development, newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

    Sources indicate that woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

    Sources indicate that play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

    Recent findings suggest that time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

    In a recent development, rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

    According to recent reports, leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

    Sources indicate that good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

    Recent findings suggest that bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

    Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

    Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

    Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

    Corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

    Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

    Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

    Industry observers note that the scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

    Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

    Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

    It has been revealed that newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

    Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

    Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

    Recent findings suggest that that was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

    Recent findings suggest that good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

    Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

    The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

    In a recent development, bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

    Recent findings suggest that on the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

    Recent findings suggest that A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

    In a recent development, leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a big threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

    Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

    It has been revealed that newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

    Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

    In a recent development, leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

    Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

    There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

    Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

    Industry observers note that fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

    Newcastle get the game under way.

    Industry observers note that matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

    Recent findings suggest that the former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

    Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane.

    Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst.

    Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa.

    Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave.

    Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq.

    Newcastle United continue their preparations for the new season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

    According to recent reports, latest manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

    Industry observers note that “It’s a challenge, a major challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle mentioned.

    “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

    Recent findings suggest that “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

    The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

    He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

    “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

    “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

    Jaissle remarked he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

    According to recent reports, “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

    “The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.
    • On platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026.
    • Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    On platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    It has been revealed that on Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note said.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    In that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.
