    #107736. How have the Heat turned their season around? Giannis and Bam are on fire, but that's not all

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1402 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    How have the Heat turned their season around? Giannis and Bam are on fire, but that's not all

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1402 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light.
    • Recent findings suggest that how have they turned things around?
    • Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light. It initially came against weaker opponents, with wins over the Pacers, Clippers, Jazz and Kings getting them back near .500. But these back-to-back wins over Cleveland (on Friday) and Detroit (on Saturday) put a real stamp on this stretch. After all the panic, Miami has won seven of nine and is tied for the East's No. 4 seed entering this week.

    Recent findings suggest that how have they turned things around? Let's take a look at four major reasons.

    Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins. The concerns over their offensive fit -- as relative non-shooters who operate largely in the same spots -- have quieted, but also a good bit of this production is coming independent of one another as Erik Spoelstra is staggering their minutes between the start of each half and fourth-quarter closing time.

    With shooters all around, Adebayo and Antetokounmpo are free to attack maximum interior space and exploit soft midrange spots, which has been the bread and butter of this run.

    Every mid range jumper from Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo against Cleveland last night: pic.twitter.com/jeamVaSLhk.

    As pointed out by Couper Moorhead of NBA.com, the Heat face more drop-coverage defense (when the substantial who's guarding the ball screener falls back toward the rim rather than stepping up to the level of the screen or even higher to contest the shooter coming off the screen) than any other offense in the league. That's because nobody fears Miami's pull-up 3-point shooters, and because Giannis and Bam are such forceful attackers of the rim.

    Industry observers note that the soft spot is in between, outside the restricted circle but inside the 3-point line, or even better inside the free-throw line. It's the dreaded midrange zone, where defenses are happy to, concede shots to players like Giannis and Bam, and right now they are both knocking these supposedly inefficient looks down at ridiculous rates.

    Sources indicate that these are by far career-high percentages for both guys, and they are coming on career-high frequencies from these zones (over 30% of their total shot attempts in the 3-10 range). Over these last nine games, Giannis is a scorching 22 for 33 from 10-19 feet while Adebayo -- who has also been the best post scorer in the league at 1.26 PPP on 4.8 post-ups per game -- is 30 for 44 from 5-14 feet.

    Recent findings suggest that they are absolutely wearing these outer-paint shots out, and if defenses keep with the drop coverage, these shots are likely to remain consistently available. It's not to say they'll keep making them at this rate, of course. But to have established these go-zones is a substantial step for Miami's half-court offense, because we all know how dangerous they are in the open floor as the highest-frequency and second-highest-scoring transition team.

    Now add in the fact that Miami kills teams on the glass with Giannis and Bam on the court (over these last nine, they are grabbing 78.7 percent of all available defensive rebounds and 37.8% of all offensive rebounds, both of which would lead the league), and in the turnover battle, and what you have is a Heat team that is getting a lot more true shot attempts than its opponents (almost 10 more per 100 possessions).

    That is everything in today's possession-obsessed NBA. Get up more shots than your opponent by generating second-chance opportunities on the offensive boards and by creating more turnovers than you cough up, and you're in a good spot. Make those extra shots at the rate Miami is right now, and you're almost unbeatable.

    Mitchell has gone from a guy perhaps playing to stay in the league, or at least in an NBA rotation, to a current top-three Most Improved Player candidate at FanDuel (+900). He's blowing his previous production away.

    The Heat are a low-volume pick-and-roll team for the same reasons they're a prime candidate for drop coverage: They don't have those kinds of pull-up shooters. Mitchell can punish drops with pull-up 3s on occasion (8 for 20 so far, per Synergy), but more importantly he's the one most often hitting Bam and Giannis in those soft-pocket midrange spots we talked about -- in addition to the rim rolls, cuts and kick-out 3s that open up as he breaches the paint, often in transition.

    Of Mitchell's 119 assists so far, 55 have gone to Giannis and Bam, and he has directly set up a 3-point make 37 times. Those 9.2 assists per game lead the league among qualified players, and the 257 points his assists have generated rank second only to Trae Young's 260, per PBP Stats. Young is making $49 million this year. Mitchell is making $12 million.

    In a recent development, then there is the shooting. Mitchell has steadily improved from range throughout his career, but this season he's on fire at 43% on catch-and-shoot 3s, per Synergy, as part of Miami's spacing around Bam and Giannis. We saw all of Mitchell's tools in his 22-point/17-assist masterpiece against Cleveland.

    Davion Mitchell ABSURD statline vs Cavs: 22 PTS | 5 REB | 17 AST | 7/14 FG | 66 TS% pic.twitter.com/b0d8I1XHDy.

    Industry observers note that thompson isn't the player he was in his prime. His defense has especially declined, and he's not going to be putting up any more 37-point quarters. But he's still a sniper.

    Thompson is splashing 42% on almost 10 3s a game, and his 48 total 3-pointers rank third league-wide, and his 15.3 PPG are the most he's averaged since leaving Golden State. He's been especially hot of late, averaging 20 PPG on 48/45 shooting splits over his last seven games.

    Klay Thompson was amazing vs the Pistons26 PTS - 4 AST - 6 3PM - 10/17 FGM Found a new home pic.twitter.com/JvQju9Hais.

    Over the last seven games, Miami is plus-11.7 with Thompson on the court and minus-3.7 when he's off. That's the best split on the team. The starting lineup of Mitchell, Bam, Giannis, Thompson and Pelle Larsson (who has been significant in this turnaround, too, since his promotion to the first five), the Heat are outscoring opponents by 23 points per 100 possessions, and Thompson has been particularly effective playing alongside Giannis. With those two on the court as Bam rests, Miami is drumming teams by 31.6 points per 100, per Databallr.

    Recent findings suggest that miami's defense was expected to be a strength, and when people looked up and saw a bottom-barrel rating, it was jarring. Some of that, if not most of it, could be attributed to inordinately hot shooting by their opponents, which wasn't likely to continue. And indeed it hasn't.

    Through the first seven games, Miami opponents were shooting 41.8% from 3 and 50% from the midrange, per Cleaning the Glass. That made for a 58.7 effective field-goal percentage, despite Miami's defense registering a top-three expected eFG% (52.9) based on the shots they were surrendering, per Cleaning the Glass.

    According to recent reports, translation: the Heat were, and are, forcing generally inefficient shots, but to start the year those shots were going in at a rate of almost 6% better than expected. That was the worst, or unluckiest, mark in the league, however you want to look at it.

    It has been revealed that cut to this four-game win streak, over which opponents are down to 35.2% from 3 with a 53.9 eFG% against an expected 54%, per CTG. That's in part because Miami has cut the number of wide-open 3s (nearest defender at least six feet away) it was allowing to start the year almost in half (to start, they were surrendering 16 wide-open 3s every night, but over this four-game winning streak they are down to 9.1, stingiest in the league). Even better, their opponents have come down from a 45.5% conversion rate on those wide-open 3s to 40%.

    It has been revealed that all of which is to say, Miami's opponent shooting is coming back to earth. Hot shooting can render any defense helpless, but over time, if you're forcing a team into tough shots from tough spots, the averages are going to swing back your way eventually. Miami is starting to see that happen.

    #107734. 10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1629 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1629 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that this Friday, Nov.
    • Dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary.
    • With that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that this Friday, Nov. 20, is an vital date on MLB's offseason calendar. It is the deadline for teams to offer 2027 contracts to their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players. The player does not have to sign by Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline, but he must be offered a contract. If he's not, the player is considered non-tendered and immediately becomes a free agent.

    Dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary. Adolis García, Nathaniel Lowe, Alek Manoah, and Christopher Morel were among the notable non-tenders last offseason. Go back a few years and major names like Cody Bellinger and Kyle Schwarber were non-tendered.

    With that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors. You can be sure these teams will scour the trade market for these players and try to get something back before making the non-tender official.

    Projected salary: $11.1 million (team control through 2028).

    Duran was a non-tender candidate even before the Jake Bauers signing pushed him out of the everyday lineup. There is no such thing as too many good players, but the Red Sox now have two first basemen (Bauers and Willson Contreras) and four outfielders (Duran, Wilyer Abreu, Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela). Mickey Gasper and Masataka Yoshida are still around too. That's eight players for five lineup spots (first base, DH, three outfield spots). On any given day, three of those guys will be on the bench. Duran, who got MVP votes in 2024, had a 20-20 season in 2026, but it came with a ballooning strikeout rate and a .266 on-base percentage. He has been on the trade block for close to two years now and the writing is on the wall. If the Red Sox are unable to trade Duran this week, there's a real chance he'll get non-tendered Friday given his hefty salary projection.

    Projected salary: $7.7 million (team control through 2028).

    In a recent development, former No. 1 overall draft picks have been non-tendered in the past (Tim Beckham most recently), just not by the team that drafted them. Non-tendering Torkelson would be a tough look for the Tigers even though he has not developed into the impact hitter he was projected to be coming out of Arizona State. Simply put, the salary is beginning to outweigh the production. Torkelson, 27, is a 25-30 homer bat with one of the league's highest strikeout rates, middling on-base percentages, and no secondary value (defense, baserunning, etc.). That remarked, the Tigers do not have an obvious replacement first baseman ready to step in (Colt Keith was the backup in 2026). That, plus the fact that Torkelson has No. 1 pick pedigree, could keep him in Detroit another year.

    Projected salary: $2.3 million (team control through 2029).

    The American League Rookie of the Year in 2024, Gil has battled injuries and ineffectiveness in the two seasons since. The swing-and-miss rate on his fastball went from an elite 28.5% in 2024 to a below-average 18.8% in 2025 and 17.4% in 2026. Gil, 28, spent time in Triple-A this past season and the Yankees moved him into the bullpen late in the year, where the results were so-so. The salary projection is a pittance, particularly for a team with Fresh York's payroll, though Gil is now out of minor-league options (he must pass through waivers to go to Triple-A) and doesn't have an obvious role. Because he is a pitcher and breathing, and also has a major award win in the not-too-distant past, the Yankees might be able to find a trade partner this week. If not, Gil is a definite non-tender candidate.

    Projected salary: $7.6 million (team control through 2028).

    In a recent development, A fan favorite and an All-Star this past season, Clement crashed hard in the second half, and the fact of the matter is he has a .295 on-base percentage in his three full seasons with the Blue Jays. Also, the soon-to-be 31-year-old's defensive numbers tumbled this year. Clement's contact skills are elite and he's a versatile, high-energy player. As a utility guy, he's an ace. As an everyday player, he's stretched. Clement's projected salary is hefty for a utility player, particularly one with limited offensive upside who no longer reliably catches the baseball. My guess is the Blue Jays will keep him and live with the salary, but it's not an obvious decision.

    Projected salary: $5.1 million (team control through 2028).

    Similar to Torkelson, non-tendering a former No. 1 overall pick would be a tough look for the Twins, but a clean break might be best for all involved at this point. Lewis, 27, has trended down since his boffo second half in 2023, enough that he was sent to Triple-A for a spell this summer. He's also moved down the defensive spectrum from third base to first base. It's not due to a lack of effort; Lewis is a major tinkerer who has tried all sorts of swing adjustments. It just hasn't come together. A fresh start elsewhere, away from the spotlight of former No. 1 pick and face of the franchise, might be best for him. The budget-conscious Twins could then reallocate the projected $5.1 million elsewhere on the roster. Right now, they can't count on Lewis to hit or have a meaningful impact defensively.

    Projected salary: $3.4 million (team control through 2028).

    In 2023, Gorman slugged 27 home runs and looked like one of baseball's top young power hitters. In the three seasons since, he has not come close to repeating that success. The hope was that moving him to third base, his natural position, would unlock Gorman's offense following the Nolan Arenado trade. That didn't happen, and Gorman spent a significant chunk of the summer in Triple-A, where he continued to have a hard time making contact. Now 26, Gorman has a minor-league option remaining and can go to Triple-A again in 2027, but the signs are not subtle. The Cardinals are reportedly seeking a stopgap third baseman until top prospect Jesús Báez is ready, which would likely not be the case if they had any belief in Gorman. That projected $3.4 million salary is a high price for a reclamation project ticketed for the minors.

    Projected salary: $6.9 million (team control through 2028).

    Right-handed power is in short supply throughout baseball and Burger, 31 in April, has hit at least 28 home runs in three of the last four years. He is a one-tool player, though. The home runs come with low batting averages, low on-base percentages, higher-than-average strikeout rates, and little to no defensive or baserunning value. Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young said his team lacked "grit and toughness," whatever that means, and indicated he wants more hitters who grind out at-bats. That's not Burger, who can hit the ball a mile but is not known for making life tough on pitchers. The $6.9 million projection could be deemed too pricey for a player with such a limited skill set.

    Projected salary: $6.6 million (team control through 2027).

    Doval went from the Yankees to the Pirates at the trade deadline, then from the Pirates to the Giants on waivers in September. He's a former All-Star who led the National League in saves in 2023, two things that have boosted his arbitration salaries. Since 2023, Doval has been a middle reliever who was on the outside of the Circle of Trust™ more often than not. The 29-year-old righty still throws very hard. There's nothing wrong with his arm. It's hard to believe he gets hit as hard as he does sometimes. Doval earned $6.1 million in 2026 and a player cannot have a salary cut by more than 20% during his team control years. That would set Doval's minimum 2027 salary at $4.88 million. I wonder if the Giants would offer him a pay cut, say $5.5M or so, and tell him it's either that or a non-tender. That happens a few times a year around the league.

    Projected salary: $6.5 million (team control through 2027).

    A fan favorite in San Diego -- "Ho-ly Sheets!" chants are commonplace during his at-bats at Petco Park -- Sheets has fallen by the wayside a bit with the Padres, so much so that he started just one of their six postseason games this year. The 30-year-old is a platoon player who is good against righties more than great and is a defensive liability at both first base and left field. Realistically, Sheets is a platoon DH, and teams rarely pay well for that role unless they're confident they will get big offensive numbers. In the grand scheme of things, the projected $6.5 million isn't much. It is top-of-the-market dollars for this skill set, however.

    Projected salary: $1.4 million (team control through 2029).

    Two years ago, Blanco threw a no-hitter in his eighth career start. This year, he was so far out of the picture that he pitched once in Houston's last 12 games (two innings at the end of a 13-2 blowout), and the Astros opted to start Peter Lambert on two days' rest with a postseason spot on the line in Game 162. Blanco, who is older than you may realize (he turned 33 in August), returned from Tommy John surgery this summer and had a rough go of it. The pitching-needy Astros could send him to Triple-A next season, as he has a minor-league option remaining, but his stuff was diminished after surgery, and again, they didn't trust him late in the year. You would be surprised at how many cheap pitchers get non-tendered every year. Blanco could join them this week.

    2027 Baseball Hall of Fame ballot released: 8 things to know, including newcomers, trends and a prediction

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1166 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.
    • According to recent reports, the full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman.
    • Industry observers note that as a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.

    According to recent reports, the full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman. Newcomers to the ballot are in bold.

    Industry observers note that as a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class. Those who get at least 5% of the vote can remain on the ballot the following year, and so on, for a maximum of 10 voting cycles. Players who are on the ballot for 10 years without getting 75% of the vote, in addition to players not getting 5% of the vote, fall off the ballot in ensuing years, though that doesn't mean the doors to the Hall are permanently shut.

    The results will be unveiled on Jan. 19, with the induction set for Cooperstown over the summer.

    Here's everything else you need to know about the Baseball Hall of Fame this offseason.

    As alluded to earlier, there are two different votes each offseason. The BBWAA vote is for former players who have been retired from Major League Baseball for at least five years. It's the most common method in mainstream Hall of Fame ballot discussions. When you hear stuff like "first-ballot Hall of Famer," it means via the BBWAA vote.

    Players who don't make it via the BBWAA vote can get extra chances via committees. That's how, for example, Jeff Kent made it last year. Formerly called the Veterans Committee, the Hall of Fame now uses Era Committees, which are divided into two categories: contemporary baseball (1980 to present) and classic (prior to 1980). The contemporary ballot is then split into two, one for players and one for non-players like umpires, executives, pioneers and managers.

    Sure enough, this time around, it is a non-player Contemporary Baseball Committee, which looks at "managers, umpires and executives whose most significant career impact was realized since 1980.".

    Industry observers note that we'll dive further into this group as we get closer to the Dec. 6 vote.

    It has been revealed that giants legend Buster Posey joins the ballot, and he's one of those cases where I don't think a bunch of people need to delve deeply into his numbers. More than statistics, sometimes we get "feel" guys, as in, you just know he's a Hall of Famer. Posey qualifies there, I would think, for 75% of the electorate. We'll obviously do a deeper dive in the coming weeks, but even without the longevity component (Posey only played in parts of 12 MLB seasons), I think he's in.

    As for the rest of the first-timers, the best case would be Jon Lester. Given the way a lot of similar starting pitchers have been treated in voting in recent years, my hunch is he'll be able to hang around on the ballot, but he has a major uphill battle in order to get in.

    Then you're looking at Brett Gardner, Ryan Zimmerman, Kyle Seager, the short peak of Jake Arrieta and relief work of Andrew Miller. Good players worth mentioning, of course, but they won't sniff the Hall and it seems likely all behind Posey and Lester are one-and-dones on this ballot, as they'll fall short of 5% of the vote.

    This is the sixth year for Alex Rodriguez on the ballot, which means it's the sixth time that I point out that we don't really need much time to go over his case. His numbers say he's one of the 10 best position players of all time, but his ties to PEDs are keeping him out to this point.

    He did rise from 37.1% of the vote in 2025 to 40% last time, a fresh high-water mark. The progress is too modest to believe it's trending toward him getting in, but the number this year is certainly worth watching. If he somehow makes a leap to the 50% range, a deeper conversation might be in order.

    While some voters don't mind sending in blank ballots to prove some sort of nebulous point, most impose limits on themselves. Whether it's the actual rule of 10 or some voters saying they'll only vote, for example, for a maximum of three players on any given ballot, relatively weak ballots can leave openings for the best players to show huge gains. With Carlos Beltràn and Andruw Jones getting in last year and only one strong first-year candidate, perhaps Chase Utley can benefit.

    Utley is only in his fourth year on the ballot, but he's already made significant gains:.

    Sources indicate that he only needs to add 15.9 points after jumping nearly 20 last voting cycle. The situation is ripe for Utley to either get all the way in or get close enough to where he probably makes the Hall of Fame in 2028.

    Some of us are pushing to lower the Hall of Fame standard on modern starting pitchers, given the decreases in workload and how it affects their career numbers. We might be making some headway, but it's still tough sledding. Here are the holdover starting pitchers and their standing:.

    Recent findings suggest that the bar for relievers to make the Hall of Fame is justly pretty high. We recently saw Billy Wagner make a late move and make it in his last try on the BBWAA ballot. Francisco Rodríguez has had four chances on the ballot and gotten between 7.8% and 11.8% of the vote thus far.

    Sources indicate that K-Rod ranks sixth all time in saves and has good rate stats. He's worth tracking as it relates to three active relievers. Kenley Jansen is third in saves with a similar number of innings pitched to K-Rod. Craig Kimbrel is fifth and has more than 100 fewer innings pitched. Aroldis Chapman is ninth and in the ballpark of Kimbrel in workload to this point.

    According to recent reports, if K-Rod continues to have trouble making headway toward induction, does that mean Kimbrel and Chapman will have trouble as well? What about Jansen?

    Who else is back on the ballot? A quick look:.

    Posey is a lock. If the committee era chooses Bochy, Baker and/or Sabean, that would be some nice San Francisco flavor, too, right? I'll predict that committee ballot at a later date, though.

    I'll also say Utley's good roll here continues with a relatively weak ballot (at least when you factor in what the PED stain has done to some guys).

    On the player side, my 2027 Hall of Fame class prediction is Buster Posey and Chase Utley.

    According to recent reports, hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving. In Major League Baseball, that usually means a slow news week. Those of us wanting a flurry of moves before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 are starting to lose a little hope, but hey, it's still possible. We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition.

    As for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov. 16, let's go.

    The Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner. They have extended a qualifying offer to Trevor Rogers and though he's expected to decline it, a reunion remains possible. If not, the Orioles are also reportedly interested in lefty free agents Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd and David Peterson.

    Rogers is the best option here. He finished last season with a 2.90 ERA in his last 20 starts. CBS Sports ranked him as the No. 3 free agent this offseason and the best non-Tarik Skubal pitcher on the market. Here's part of the write-up:.

    According to recent reports, rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years.

    Sources indicate that as things stand, the Orioles' rotation starts with right-handers Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Cade Povich is a left-handed option, but they'd clearly like someone else who could qualify as a frontline starter from the left-handed side.

    Former Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara has been involved in trade rumors for years and the Marlins never end up moving him. More of the same this offseason? Probably.

    "I expect Sandy to be on the Marlins next year," general manager Peter Bendix told MLB Network.

    Sources indicate that alcantara, 31, was 13-11 with a 3.87 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 153 strikeouts in an MLB-best 214 innings last season. He also grabbed three saves down the stretch as the Marlins started experimenting with using starters in relief on their bullpen day between starts. The 2022 Cy Young winner missed all of 2024 after having Tommy John surgery and started to show flashes of his old self last season. He's now making $21 million in 2027 before hitting free agency.

    If the Marlins contend, he'll surely stay put, but if they fall out of contention, it'll be another round of trade rumors.

    Sources indicate that free agent left-hander A.J. Minter is getting a lot of interest, per MLB Network. Coming off a season in which he was productive for both the Mets and Twins (in all, a 2.56 ERA, 1.05 WHIP and 41 strikeouts in 45 ⅔ innings), he's being chased by at least the Blue Jays, Nationals, Phillies, Rangers and Royals.

    Though he's closed on occasion, Minter has been a quality setup man for most of his 10 MLB years, especially with the Braves in the 2020-24 range. He has good playoff numbers, too, with a 2.88 ERA in 20 career postseason appearances.

    The Brewers have acquired right-handed reliever Ryan Walker from the Giants for two minor-league pitchers, the team confirmed late Sunday. Walker, 30, was up and down in his four years with the Giants, which included time as a closer. He had a 1.91 ERA, 10 saves and 2.8 WAR in 2024, but lost the job of closer during a sub-par 2025 season. Last year, he pitched to a 7.16 ERA and 1.81 WHIP in 32 ⅔ innings.

    We have plenty of examples of the Brewers buying low on a player and ending up getting the best version of him, so Walker is the latest to keep an eye on here.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Almost anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 11 of the 2026 season showcased the limits of the league's parity.

    In the Houston Texans' (4-6) 26-3 road win on the road over the torn-down Indianapolis Colts (3-8), three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor went for just 21 yards rushing on 11 carries. It marked an unfathomable 21 consecutive games without 100 yards rushing in a game, the worst drought of his career. Meanwhile, quarterback Daniel Jones just polished off his sixth straight game with an interception, the longest streak by a Colts player since Curtis Painter was filling in for an injured Peyton Manning in 2011.

    Industry observers note that meanwhile, Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud threw two of his three touchdown passes for 20-plus air yards after having two combined in his first nine games of the 2026 season. Stroud's seven-game streak of multiple total touchdowns is now the longest in Texans history.

    Recent findings suggest that what surprises could occur across the rest of the NFL's Week 11 slate? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.

    Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, made his debut as an NFL starting quarterback against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 10. That made Mendoza the first No. 1 overall pick in NFL history to make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion, per CBS Sports Research. He held his own, completing 17 of his 29 throws for 143 yards while also adding 22 yards and a rushing touchdown on six carries. Despite being sacked six times, Mendoza and the Raiders only lost by eight points, 21-13.

    Recent findings suggest that after adjusting to the pace of the NFL game against the Seahawks, Mendoza and the Raiders will head to Empower Field at Mile High Stadium in Denver and emerge victorious against the Broncos. Denver quarterback Bo Nix doesn't scare any defense, ranking last in the league in air yards per pass attempt (5.6). For whatever reason, he can't or won't pull the trigger on throws down the field. Five-time Pro Bowl Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby will do enough to spook Nix while Mendoza helps Las Vegas' offense score just enough points for the 10.5-point underdogs, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, to emerge victorious on Sunday.

    In a recent development, tony Pollard is ascending to fresh heights at the age of 29 and in the final year of his three-year, $21.75 million contract with the Tennessee Titans. Across his last three games, Pollard has produced 279 yards rushing, 112 yards receiving and six total touchdowns. Even though the Titans had a Week 9 bye, Pollard still ranks in the top 10 in rushing yards, rushing touchdowns, receiving touchdowns and total touchdowns by a running back since Week 7. His five rushing touchdowns are tied for the most in the NFL in this span with Bucky Irving, and his six scrimmage touchdowns in this stretch are tied for the most in the league with Christian McCaffrey.

    Recent findings suggest that pollard now has his sights set on scoring a touchdown in four consecutive games for the first time in his eight-season NFL career. And just in time for his first matchup with the Dallas Cowboys, the team that drafted him in the fourth round of the 2019 NFL Draft and the team he called home for his first five seasons. His homecoming on Sunday at AT&T Stadium will mark Pollard's first career game against the Cowboys, and he'll have a special day against a Dallas defense that is in total disarray after the half-firing of first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Wednesday. Parker retains his title as defensive coordinator, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer stripped him of defensive play-calling duties and gave them to senior assistant Mike Pettine, a 60-year-old who was retired and vacationing in Italy just a few months ago. Pettine last worked as a defensive play-caller in the NFL in 2020, his final season as the defensive coordinator of the Green Bay Packers.

    Pollard will join Jahmyr Gibbs (twice this season), Bijan Robinson (Week 3 at the Green Bay Packers) and McCaffrey (Week 10 at the Cowboys) as just the fourth player in the entire league this season with 200-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in a game on Sunday against his old friends.

    It has been revealed that detroit Lions Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs decimated the New England Patriots for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on seven catches), the most in a game by any player this season. He also added two rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the Patriots in Munich, Germany. What can the league's rushing yards (1,000), scrimmage yards (1,384) and scrimmage touchdowns (13) leader do for Week 11 as an encore against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the NFL's No. 1 run defense?

    According to recent reports, the Bucs  are giving up just 79.2 rushing yards per game allowed. But Gibbs will steamroll Buccaneers Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and Co. for 120 yards rushing, something that hasn't been done to Tampa Bay since TreVeyon Henderson did so in Week 10 of last season. Do you know who produced the next-most-recent occurrence against the Buccaneers? That's right, it was Gibbs in Week 7 of the 2025 season when he went off for 136 yards rushing and two touchdowns on 17 carries in a 24-9 victory. He'll go over 120 again against the NFL's best run defense on Sunday.

    The Miami Dolphins head up north to Buffalo to face the 8-1 Bills, the AFC's No. 1 seed, as 16.5-point underdogs per DraftKings Sportsbook. Essentially, the expectation is for the Dolphins to lose by three scores. It's understandable to see why. Bills quarterback Josh Allen has the most total touchdowns in a player's first 10 seasons (325) despite 2026 being just his ninth NFL season. Allen alone has more career playoff touchdowns (39) than Miami's active roster (38) does in the regular season. The Dolphins active roster's 38 combined career touchdowns are the fewest in the NFL by any team's active roster by nearly 50 touchdowns — the Arizona Cardinals are the next-lowest with 85.

    Buffalo is tied for the best record in the NFL along with the San Francisco 49ers at 8-1, while Miami is tied for the worst record at 1-8 with the Titans and the Los Angeles Chargers. However, the Dolphins will lose by only one score on Sunday.

    How is this possible? Well, the Bills have outscored their opponents 90-28 in their last three games while facing five backup quarterbacks: Tyler Huntley, Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Max Brosmer and Cade Klubnik. Yes, the Dolphins are starting one too — 2025 sixth-round pick Kyle McCord — with Malik Willis sidelined, but McCord had a decent debut at theIndianapolis Colts in Week 10. He threw for 209 yards, the second most in an NFL debut in Dolphins history, on 17-of-32 passing with a rushing touchdown and one lost fumble. Rookie third-round wide receiver Caleb Douglas' 367 yards receiving in six games is the most in a player's first six career games in Dolphins history.

    According to recent reports, no team in the last 20 years has seen a higher rate of their snaps (28.8%) go to rookies than the 2026 Dolphins have. They don't know what they don't know. That's why they're going to lose by just one possession against the mighty Bills in Buffalo in Week 11.

    Industry observers note that chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams returns from a Week 10 bye out for blood after throwing four interceptions in Week 9 against the Buccaneers. That snapped his 36-game streak without multiple interceptions, the fourth-longest streak by a starting quarterback since 1950. Williams will be itching to go deep downfield to wide receivers Luther Burden and Rome Odunze to atone for his sloppy play in the last time out.

    Sources indicate that williams' problem is that he is facing one of the best pass-rushing teammate duos in football against the Latest Orleans Saints. Saints edge rushers Carl Granderson (8.5 sacks, tied for the second most in the NFL) and Chase Young (8.0 sacks, tied for the fourth-most) have combined for 16.5 sacks, tied for the most of any teammate pass rush duo this season along with the Minnesota Vikings' Andrew Van Ginkel (8.5) and Dallas Turner (8.0).

    The Saints' defense as a whole hasn't been stellar this season, profiling as the league's No. 25 scoring defense (26.2 points per game allowed), but they'll combine to sack Williams a season-high five times on Sunday. Williams' 3.35-second average time to throw is the longest in the NFL among the league's 31 qualified quarterbacks, which will doom him against Granderson, Young and the Latest Orleans defense.

    #107722. Industry News: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

    📅 22 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 25m • 📚 Deep Dive (4964 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

    📅 22 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4964 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur.
    • Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.
    • But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

    Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

    But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

    The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

    The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

    There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

    Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

    It has been revealed that sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

    Industry observers note that “He is a top player, no doubt about it,” mentioned head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

    “He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

    A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

    Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

    Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the fresh season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

    Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a massive cheer from the home fans.

    Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

    He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

    Sources indicate that richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

    Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

    Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

    De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

    This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

    Sources indicate that bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

    In a recent development, once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

    Recent findings suggest that michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU.

    Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

    According to recent reports, igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h.

    De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more new faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

    Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

    But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

    Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that substantial-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his upcoming-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

    Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on upcoming players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

    Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow fresh signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

    Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

    His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

    Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

    Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the significant spenders.

    It has been revealed that that is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

    The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

    De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

    In a recent development, spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

    Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

    Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

    Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

    Sources indicate that “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

    Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This season's NBA Rookie of the Year race has the potential to be one of the closest in league history. While there is no 65-game requirement to win the award — unlike MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and All-NBA honors — playing as many games as possible will be paramount this season in order to claim Rookie of the Year.

    That's why Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson faces an uphill climb to win the honor after fracturing his right hand earlier this month. Wilson is set to miss the next 3-5 weeks and will likely lose serious ground to others in his class. He at the moment has the sixth-best odds (+4000) on FanDuel Sportsbook to win Rookie of the Year.

    During the first month of the season, three players have separated themselves at the top: Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer, and Darius Acuff Jr. While it's not a guarantee one of those players wins it, if the season ended today, those would be the top vote-getters.

    Darryn Peterson and AJ Dybantsa — the first two picks of the 2026 NBA Draft — have some ground to make up during the next four months to get back in the mix.

    Industry observers note that with the regular season almost a quarter of the way complete, let's dive into our first Rookie of the Year rankings. All odds via FanDuel.

    With Steph Curry out, Lendeborg has continued to step up. The oldest player drafted in the first round is coming off a lackluster showing against the Spurs in the NBA Cup, but before that he had three straight games of 23+ points. He is shooting 48.6% from the field and 41.4% from 3. Lendeborg didn't start shooting 3s on a consistent basis until he got to Michigan last season, so knocking down that percentage on 5.4 attempts per night is a positive sign. Fourteen games into the season, Lendeborg is the favorite.

    It has been revealed that boozer's raw stats aren't as good as Lendeborg's or even Acuff's, but his impact goes well beyond the box score. His feel for the game is elite for a 19-year-old. Boozer keeps getting better and better as a processor as he continues to log more minutes. The Grizzlies have been one of the league's surprising teams this season. Boozer deserves a ton of credit for that. He wins everywhere he goes, whether at the high school, college, or professional level.

    Acuff just turned 20 last week. In 13 games as a teenager, he averaged 25.5 points per game and became the first teenager in NBA history to score at least 275 points and dish out 80 assists in his first 11 games. Acuff is a special offensive talent who is being asked to do more than any rookie in his class. Sacramento is a very bad basketball team, but Acuff makes the Kings somewhat fun to watch. That's a huge credit to him.

    Sources indicate that the Jazz have been decimated by injuries this season and are at the moment riding a 12-game losing streak. The one bright side amidst some very bad basketball is how good Peterson has been during that stretch. Peterson had a five-game stretch in which he scored 20 points in each game and shot the ball well from 3. Peterson is the future of Utah's franchise, so getting him as many reps as possible on and off the ball should be the priority.

    Recent findings suggest that dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick, is averaging 14 shot attempts per game during his first 10 appearances as a pro. He should be taking even more shots. The way the Wizards are using him is confusing at times. Dybantsa is in somewhat of a weird situation because of the Wizards' roster. Washington handed Trae Young a huge contract this offseason that is already aging poorly. Dybantsa should be the focus of the offense. He should be touching the ball and shooting it even more than he is already. I have been impressed with Dybantsa's defense this season.

    NFL exploring possibility of implementing latest travel rules for international games

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (696 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With the NFL's uptick in international games over the last few years, there's no rule requiring a team to arrive in a foreign city by a certain date before a game, but that could change.
    • The NFL is right now exploring a new travel policy that would require each team to spend a minimum number of nights in an international city.
    • In a recent development, "At the moment, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," O'Reilly stated.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With the NFL's uptick in international games over the last few years, there's no rule requiring a team to arrive in a foreign city by a certain date before a game, but that could change. That could change soon.

    The NFL is right now exploring a new travel policy that would require each team to spend a minimum number of nights in an international city. In an interview this week with The Athletic, NFL executive VP of club business Peter O'Reilly confirmed that a change could be coming.

    In a recent development, "At the moment, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," O'Reilly stated. "It is something that we'll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It's something we'll look at.".

    It's no surprise the NFL is thinking hard about this topic, especially after what happened in Week 1 during the league's first regular-season game in Australia between the 49ers and the Rams. The 49ers decided to fly out a full week before the game so they could acclimate to the 17-hour time difference. Leaving early also allowed the team to fully immerse themselves in Australian culture.

    On the other hand, the Rams infamously didn't arrive until the last minute: They landed in Melbourne at about 7 a.m. ET on Thursday morning, leaving them less than 30 hours until their game with the 49ers kicked off.

    Sources indicate that the Rams traveled late so that their players wouldn't have to adjust to Australian time, but the blueprint backfired. The Rams looked slow and tired during a 27-7 loss.

    If the NFL does implement a minimum-night rule, it likely won't be anything dramatic. The rule that would make the most sense is having teams arrive at least two nights in advance. For a game in Europe, that would mean a team would have to leave Thursday night to arrive Friday.

    That exact travel initiative was not only popular this year, but also successful. In fact, teams traveling to Europe went 4-0 this year when arriving on Friday. The Steelers, Texans, Colts, and Jaguars (for their first London game) all arrived Friday morning for their international game, and all four teams won. It's hard to imagine the NFL creating a rule to eliminate something that's working well for teams, so if the league implements a new travel policy, it likely won't be a massive change.

    Industry observers note that since international play started in 2007, there are only three instances of a team showing up the day before a game in a city at least five time zones away, and the Rams were involved in two of them. The Rams arrived on Saturday in London for a 35-7 blowout win over the Jaguars in 2025, which is why they likely felt good about arriving the day before the game in Australia this year. The Eagles ended up copying the Rams' strategy for their game in London this year, arriving on Saturday for their matchup against the Jags, which ended up being a dramatic 19-17 loss.

    There were a total of nine international games this year, and the final one will be played in Mexico City on Sunday night between the Vikings and the 49ers. If the NFL does implement a new travel policy, it will be interesting to see whether it includes games like this that are geographically closer to the United States. The Vikings are flying down to the game on Saturday because the flight from Minnesota to Mexico City is only about 4.5 hours and there's no time zone change, so it's not necessarily a reason to travel early (The stadium in Mexico City does have an altitude of 7,350 feet, so it could make sense to travel early to get acclimated to that, but the Vikings decided not to go that route).

    Under the current CBA, the NFL is allowed to schedule up to 10 international games for 2027, and if the league hits that number, it will certainly be interesting to see if a latest travel policy is in place for next season.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that as we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec.
    • The decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No.
    • "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that as we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec. 1 lockout of the players by MLB owners, we might see an accelerated pace of activity soon. The most tantalizing possibility is that ace and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the undisputed top talent on the free agent market this winter, will sign before the sport shuts down for an indeterminate amount of time.

    The decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No. 1 free agent of the 2026-27 class, and it's not an especially close call. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He showed few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    Will he set the record for the biggest contract ever signed by a pitcher? Will Skubal fetch the highest average annual salary for a pitcher? Will he top $400 million? Those are all reasonable questions to ask. First, though, there's a question to be asked about the teams that are already pursuing him the most vigorously. That question is, which team needs him the most? We're restricting our discussion to the five teams that have been most reliably linked to Skubal so far this offseason. We're already hearing reports of surprise teams, and it's always possible a surprise late bidder will enter the fray and even win his signature, but for now, these five clubs are the favorites. This, then, is an ordering of those teams based on which desperately needs a talent like Skubal in order to reach their goals in 2027 and beyond. Let's get to it, in order from "needs him the most" to "needs him but not as urgently as the teams ahead of them" ….

    According to recent reports, the Cubs are in contention mode and in need of roster improvements if they're going to run down the world champion Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central. The rotation is without question the most pressing need for Chicago. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, David Peterson, and deadline acquisition Clay Holmes are all free agents. Justin Steele hasn't taken the mound at the major-league level since early in the 2025 season thanks to UCL surgery and a halting recovery process. While he's expected to be ready for 2027, he's not exactly a known quantity right now. Young upsider Cade Horton may not be back until midseason after undergoing Tommy John surgery, and Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery, may be on a similar timeline. So, yes, the Cubs need a lot of rotation help, and Skubal would give them the true frontline ace they'd lack even if everyone were healthy. Unfortunately for the Cubs fans, it sounds like the Ricketts aren't willing to be truly competitive for his services.

    Coming off the grave disappointments of 2026, the Mets could certainly use a headline-grabbing addition to improve their chances in 2027 and inspire a surely disaffected fan base. Beyond that, the Mets need more starting pitching to accompany promising young Nolan McLean. Christian Scott seems like a lock, but he doesn't project as a frontliner. They have some depth options for the back end, but they need a true needle-mover like Skubal at the very front. That's especially the case in what figures to be a hotly competitive NL East in 2027. Thus far, David Stearns and owner Steve Cohen sound committed to making a good-faith run at Skubal.

    The Padres have a lot of work to do if they're going to earn a fourth straight playoff appearance. Speaking of which, the rotation is crying out for help right about now. They lost Dylan Cease to free agency last winter, and this time Michael King may be bound elsewhere, too. The Pads declined their club option on Nick Pivetta, and while they hope to bring him back on more favorable terms, there's no guarantee they'll be able to do that. Yes, Joe Musgrove will be back, but how much can he give them and how effective will he be? They'll need even more help if Adrian Morejon, a lockdown bulk reliever and possible starter-conversion project, signs elsewhere. Skubal's made to order, and signing the top talent on the market would be a strong signal by new owners José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones that the team's recent tradition of spending and contending won't be fading away.

    It has been revealed that the Dodgers self-evidently needed Skubal enough to acquire him from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the deadline and do so at significant cost. On paper, the Dodgers aren't as desperate for rotation help as the teams ahead of them on this list, but there's still a need. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is a certifiable ace, but behind him Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are established health and durability risks. Shohei Ohtani is something of an unknown, at least insofar as his pitching is concerned right now, and thus far Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan have not proved worthy of being relied upon. One can squint and see the Dodgers' current championship window closing in the reasonably near future, which means that's all the more reason to push the chips in now. Retaining the elite services of Skubal would greatly aid the cause in 2027.

    Eyeball a rotation that already includes Dylan Cease, José Soriano, and Trey Yesavage, and you might think it doesn't need much more. And maybe it doesn't. As a matter of principle, though, any team with contending aspirations should be interested in a top-shelf ace when he hits the market. The Jays, who in recent years have invested in the roster at commendable levels, are no doubt dreaming of a Skubal-Cease one-two punch that would be the envy of, oh, every other team in baseball. There's also depth to think about. In particular, Cody Ponce is a bit of an unknown coming off knee surgery that ended his 2026 season in the middle of his first start. Addressing the offense probably should be more of a priority for the Jays this winter, but, again, it's Tarik Skubal, and the likes of Tarik Skubal make any team better.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Philadelphia 76ers are off to a fantastic start to the 2026-27 season at 12-3, good for first in the Eastern Conference, and perhaps most encouraging for the Sixers is that they're winning without looking like a team playing at its absolute peak.

    After a huge offseason adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, the Sixers still look like a team figuring out how best to work together, but when it comes time in the fourth quarter to find a way to win, they manage to get the job done. Tyrese Maxey is leading the way with Brown swiftly finding his rhythm, but James and Joel Embiid in particular still seem to be feeling it out early in the season.

    James, who has never averaged less than 20.9 points per game in his previous 23 seasons, is averaging just 15.1 points per game and his 44.3/22.5/71.7 shooting splits are all career lows or close to it. As James figures things out, ESPN reported that a Sixers source claimed James "asked coaches to be patient with him as he expects to find his rhythm and get his conditioning in line by December as he ramps up.".

    That report hit social media and caught James' attention, with the 41-year-old star denying ever saying that.

    ESPN didn't report a direct quote from James, and it's very possible the Sixers source offered an anecdote that paraphrased James and used the word patience when James never did. That then ended up on a social media graphic and prompted James to shoot it down.

    Sources indicate that what's fascinating here is it's not a scathing report or even anything particularly juicy. James is struggling with his shot early in the year and seems to be figuring out exactly where he fits in the offense alongside Maxey, Brown and Embiid as a scorer. He's still doing plenty of things well -- including leading the team with 6.9 assists per game and just took over third all-time in assists in NBA history -- and the Sixers are still winning even with James ice cold with his jumper, which history suggests will turn around at some point.

    Patience would be prudent from the Sixers with James, whether he wants to use that word or not, and it seems like a matter of when, not if, he gets shots to start falling and the Philly offense becomes even more dynamic.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that for the first three years of his NFL career, Detroit Lions three-time Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs was known as part of one of the NFL's best running back tandems, the "Sonic" in the Lions' "Sonic and Knuckles" duo with David Montgomery.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that for the first three years of his NFL career, Detroit Lions three-time Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs was known as part of one of the NFL's best running back tandems, the "Sonic" in the Lions' "Sonic and Knuckles" duo with David Montgomery. Today, Gibbs is showing that, as a solo act, not only can he can be the NFL's No. 1 back, but he's also laying the early groundwork to become one of the greatest running backs of all time.

    Yes, that sounds hyperbolic, but Gibbs' production is at all-time levels through three-and-a-half seasons. On an international stage in Week 10, he erupted for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on 7 catches), the most in a game by any player this season, and 2 rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the Newly introduced England Patriots in Munich, Germany. An outing like that reshuffles some NFL record boards.

    Just halfway through his fourth season, Gibbs passed Pro Football Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61 touchdowns in his first four seasons) for the most touchdowns in a player's first four seasons in NFL history (62 and counting). Gibbs is also now the first player in NFL history with 1,000 rushing yards (exactly 1,000) and 350 receiving yards (384) in a player's first nine games of a season. With an NFL-best 1,384 yards from scrimmage and a league-high13 scrimmage touchdowns in nine games, Gibbs is on pace for an NFL single-season record: 2,614 yards from scrimmage, which would smash current record holder Chris Johnson's 2,509 from the 2009 season.

    All of those feats are jaw-dropping on their own, but together they paint an all-time picture. What is perhaps most amazing about Gibbs is how consistently excellent he is, to the point that the football world is somewhat numb to his greatness. Producing 150-plus rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a game is outstanding. Six players have produced such a game this season, but five of the six have done so no more than twice. Then there is Gibbs, who has done so four times in Detroit's first nine games, making him just the fourth player in NFL history to do so. The other three are a who's who of Hall of Fame running backs: Jim Brown (1958, 1963), O.J. Simpson (1974, 1975) and Emmitt Smith (1995).

    Now, some people might feel Gibbs' historic start to his NFL career is amplified by a talent offensive ecosystem that has a five-time Pro Bowler at quarterback, Jared Goff, a four-time Pro Bowler at wide receiver (Amon-Ra St. Brown), a Pro Bowl tight end (Sam LaPorta), a four-time Pro Bowl offensive tackle (Penei Sewell), and a speedster No. 2 wide receiver (Jameson Williams). However, Gibbs and his consistent excellence power everything else in the Motor City team's offense. He ranks seventh in the league in yards before contact per rush (1.57) and eighth in yards after contact per rush (3.5) this season.

    It has been revealed that among the 27 players with at least 100 carries in 2026, Gibbs' 29.1% tackles-avoided rate is the second-best in the league, behind only Kenneth Walker III's 32.1% rate. Since Next Gen Stats began tracking explosive runs (runs of 10 or more yards) in 2016, no running back has produced more through the first 10 weeks of a season than Gibbs' 34. Prime Ezekiel Elliott in his rookie year with the Dallas Cowboys in 2016 is the closest player in this span with 29. Gibbs isn't just a cog in the Lions' machine: his juice powers the rest of the machine.

    Sources indicate that here's the cherry on top. Not even through his fourth NFL season, Gibbs has more games (two) with 250-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in his 58-game career than Barry Sanders, the running back many believe is the best pure runner ever, did in his 10-season, 153-game career.

    Week 11 gives Gibbs a chance to deliver an all-time encore performance in a matchup against Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the No. 1 run defense in the NFL (79.2 rushing yards per game allowed) this season. Get your popcorn ready as Gibbs continues to build a strong case for being the league's most productive running back ever.

He threw a career-high 145 ⅔ innings with a 4.70 ERA, though the underlying numbers (3.63 FIP and 4.50 expected ERA) were more respectable. May's 96.9 mph average fastball velocity was 15th highest among the 141 pitchers with at least 100 innings in 2026.

    According to recent reports, rotation help was a priority for a White Sox team that reached the postseason for the first time since 2021, but used openers and bullpen games regularly throughout the season. Only twice in seven postseason games did Chicago use a traditional starting pitcher. Here is the team's updated rotation depth chart:.

    Industry observers note that castillo struggled badly (30 runs in 31 innings) after coming over from the Seattle Mariners at the trade deadline, and finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder issue. His $22.75 million salary could land him in the rotation on Opening Day, though the White Sox have enough options to replace him should Castillo remain ineffective.

    Industry observers note that we ranked May as the offseason's 25th-best free agent, and the 11th-best starting pitcher. Here's a snippet of the write-up:.

    According to recent reports, may turned only 29 in September and he's topped 130 innings in back-to-back years after throwing 101 innings total around injuries, including UCL surgery, from 2021-24. Even after the injuries, May still lives in the mid-to-upper-90s with his sinker, and pitch data models are fond of his sweeper and curveball. It is not the best sign, though, that the Brewers, who know pitching as well as any team, couldn't fully unlock May after making him their big deadline rotation addition. Still, the combination of age and high-octane stuff makes him a nice upside play ...

    May made two starts and three relief appearances during Milwaukee's postseason run. If the White Sox opt to use bullpen games again next year, he is familiar and capable in that role. The signing pushes Chicago's projected 2027 payroll up to $120 million, per FanGraphs, well above the team's $102 million figure this past season.

    The White Sox went 84-78 in 2026 and became the first team in baseball history to reach the postseason after back-to-back 100-loss seasons. They lost 100 games in each of the three previous seasons, going 61-101 in 2023, 41-121 in 2024, and 60-102 in 2025.

    #107712. NBA MVP Rankings: Luka Dončić, Victor Wembanyama in a two-horse race; Stephen Curry's absence speaks volumes

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1531 w)
