    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

    Sources indicate that the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct challenges with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

    It has been revealed that all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

    According to recent reports, A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

    Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

    “It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca stated, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

    His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

    Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

    Recent findings suggest that momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

    Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

    Recent findings suggest that marco Rose, their fresh manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he mentioned. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

    His team highlighted an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

    They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

    Sources indicate that "That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

    No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

    Industry observers note that city will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a major ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “fresh Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

    There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca stated “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

    According to recent reports, of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

    Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2.

    Recent findings suggest that the Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

    Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

    Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

    Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s significant idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

    Recent findings suggest that describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

    After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

    The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

    Maikel Garcia trade grades: Mariners land Gold Glove infielder; Royals get pitching help, but with huge risks

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1270 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade.
    • In a recent development, garcia, 26, battled hand and hamstring injuries in 2026, but still managed a 1.8 WAR season in 88 games thanks to league-average offense and spectacular third base defense.
    • It has been revealed that the 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade. The Mariners have acquired third baseman Maikel Garcia in a six-player trade, the teams confirmed on Wednesday. The Royals receive righties Logan Evans and Bryce Miller and lefty Jose A. Ferrer in the deal.

    Here are the full trade details:.

    In a recent development, garcia, 26, battled hand and hamstring injuries in 2026, but still managed a 1.8 WAR season in 88 games thanks to league-average offense and spectacular third base defense. He is a year removed from a 5.6 WAR season and receiving MVP votes. Garcia is signed long-term as well. He's owed a very reasonable $52.5 million through 2030, with a club option for 2031.

    It has been revealed that the 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City. An oblique strain delayed the start to his 2026 season, but once healthy, he threw 118 ⅔ innings with a 4.17 ERA and under-the-hood numbers that were hit (3.70 expected ERA) or miss (4.41 FIP). Miller threw 180 ⅓ innings with a 2.94 ERA in 2024, and will remain under team control through 2029.

    Ferrer, 26, is a workhorse ground ball reliever with three years of control remaining. McArthur (fracture) and Evans (Tommy John) both missed 2026 with elbow surgery. McArthur pitched in four minor-league rehab games in September and should be ready for spring training. Evans has surgery in January and is expected back at midseason.

    Here now are our grades for this three-for-three swap between 2027 American League postseason hopefuls.

    The Mariners came into the offseason with an opening at third base, a glaring need to improve their defense, and more starters than rotation spots. That all came to a head in this trade. They used Miller, their least effective starter the last two seasons, and two spare parts to net a long-term solution at the hot corner in Garcia, who plays Gold Glove-caliber defense.

    Industry observers note that one player alone won't fix Seattle's defense, of course, but Garcia is a very significant step toward improving a unit that ranked 26th in defensive runs saved and 30th (by a lot) in outs above average. As for the lineup, new manager Jason Kanzler can run out something like this most days:.

    Donovan was limited to 39 games by two groin strains and a concussion this past season. He's very versatile and needn't be locked into DH. The Mariners can play Donovan in the outfield to open up DH at-bats for slugger Lazaro Montes, who hit some titanic home runs during his MLB debut in 2026. They could also move Donovan around to give others DH days.

    Sources indicate that the lineup and the defense are improved, and the Mariners still have a formidable rotation that includes Kade Anderson, Logan Gilbert, Emerson Hancock, George Kirby, and Bryan Woo. Right-hander Ryan Sloan, arguably the top pitching prospect in baseball (it's either Sloan or Anderson), is knocking on the door and figures to debut at some point in 2027.

    In a recent development, seattle will miss Ferrer in their bullpen but also have close to an entire offseason (minus a lockout) to replace him. Assuming the Mariners won't break the bank for Adrian Morejon, the free agent market still offers solid second- and third-tier lefty reliever options in A.J. Minter, Sean Newcomb, JoJo Romero, Gregory Soto, and Alex Vesia. Ferrer is a quality reliever but not irreplaceable.

    Recent findings suggest that before his elbow fracture, which ultimately required three surgeries, McArthur showed a very lively curveball and strong ground ball ability. He's a middle reliever more than a high-leverage option, but is not merely a throw-in. Langevin struck out 106 batters in 55 ⅓ Single-A relief innings thanks to his mid-90s fastball in 2026. He also walked 39 batters, however.

    Sources indicate that garcia received MVP votes a year ago thanks to a .286/.351/.449 line with 16 home runs and 23 stolen bases. He also runs some of the game's best contact rates. That's his upside and maybe 2025 was a career year, but Garcia has a reasonably high floor thanks to his defense. Getting even league-average offense moving forward makes this a win for Seattle.

    The free agent market is flush with No. 3-4 type starters and light on position players, specifically non-first base infielders. Couldn't the Royals keep Garcia and just sign a pitcher or two? There is something to be noted for Miller's cost control as an arbitration-eligible player, of course, but he hasn't been healthy and effective at the same time since 2024. That's awfully risky.

    In a recent development, evans is a quality second piece as long as he bounces back well from Tommy John surgery. He made his MLB debut with the Mariners in 2025 and underwhelmed (4.32 ERA with iffy underlying numbers in 81 ⅓ innings), though he was regarded as a strong prospect before that, someone who should hold down a rotation spot for a long time.

    Here's what FanGraphs wrote about Evans in June 2025, the last time he was prospect-eligible:.

    (His) sweeper is easily his best pitch, spins in at 2,800 rpm, and has hellacious lateral wipe. His reliance on it robs it of some bat-missing ability, and the last couple of years, the miss rate on Evans' slider has been pretty average because he's so often trying to throw it for strikes and hitters anticipate its arrival. But because Evans' fastball is fairly vulnerable, he's forced to lean on his breaking stuff ... Again, it's really only the sweeper that's plus, but Evans has a super deep repertoire, he throws a good rate of strikes and gets groundballs, and in 2024, he proved he could sustain this kind of stuff across more than 100 innings. Without a single pitch generating plus miss, he's probably not going to be a star, but he does enough to be a useful member of a significant league rotation in a no. 4/5 capacity.

    The Royals will have to wait for Evans to make an impact in their uniform because the timing of his Tommy John surgery means his rehab will extend into next spring and summer, but he is a quality second piece even if he is only a No. 4-5 starter. Cheap back-end starters are incredibly valuable and Evans should be that once his elbow is ready to go.

    Ferrer could very well wind up closing games for the Royals this season and is a quality add to the bullpen. For Kansas City, the trade boils down to three things. One, can they keep Miller healthy and get him back to his 2024 form? He's the headliner in the trade and his success is imperative. Two, will Evans turn into a reliable rotation member once his elbow is sound?

    Industry observers note that and three, was Nick Loftin's 2026 for real? The Royals believe it was, hence trading Garcia. Loftin, 28, was a Gold Glove finalist this past season and he authored a .240/.322/.388 batting line with eight home runs in 118 games. If you're sold on Loftin as a league-average hitter and Gold Glove-caliber defender, well, that's what Garcia is, just without the name value.

    It has been revealed that the Royals badly needed rotation help -- there's no arguing that -- but they also ranked 22nd in runs this year and were middle of the pack defensively despite Loftin's (and Garcia's) glovework. There's a chance Kansas City made its position player core worse with only unspectacular pitching upgrades to show for it. I understand what they did. I just don't love it.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla called on star forward Jayson Tatum to be "better" after he was called for a controversial technical foul in the closing seconds of Wednesday's 105-101 loss, which effectively sealed the game for the Denver Nuggets.
    • Recent findings suggest that "We can't put ourselves in that position to even give the refs an opportunity to interpret it a certain type of way," Mazzulla stated after the game.
    • Industry observers note that with 6.4 seconds remaining, Jamal Murray worked off a huge screen from Nikola Jokić, created space with a nasty step-back on Neemias Queta and buried a difficult jumper to give the Nuggets a three-point lead.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla called on star forward Jayson Tatum to be "better" after he was called for a controversial technical foul in the closing seconds of Wednesday's 105-101 loss, which effectively sealed the game for the Denver Nuggets.

    Recent findings suggest that "We can't put ourselves in that position to even give the refs an opportunity to interpret it a certain type of way," Mazzulla stated after the game. "Gotta be better.".

    Industry observers note that with 6.4 seconds remaining, Jamal Murray worked off a huge screen from Nikola Jokić, created space with a nasty step-back on Neemias Queta and buried a difficult jumper to give the Nuggets a three-point lead. The Celtics, who had led by as many as 17 late in the first half, still had a chance to tie, however. At least, they did, until Tatum threw the ball toward referee John Goble.

    The baseline official, Eric Dalen, immediately hit Tatum with a technical foul. Murray stepped to the line and made the free throw to put the Nuggets up by four.

    "I told [Dalen], like, I wasn't mad. Wasn't a foul on me; we just called a timeout," Tatum mentioned. "John Goble called a timeout and pointed at our bench. Thought he was looking this way, but yeah, he called a tech. For me, just find the female ref that was there, or the other ref, and whoever was probably closest, I should have just gave them the ball.".

    Jamal Murray hits a clutch jumper to extend the Nuggets the lead to 3, with 6.4 seconds remaining in regulation.The Celtics call a timeout, and Jayson Tatum throws the ball towards the ref John Goble, who wasn't looking, and receives a technical foul, which Murray converts to… pic.twitter.com/PZtzl0zs3D.

    Tatum's controversial technical capped a brutal second half for the Celtics and their star.

    After scoring 20 points in the first half to help the Celtics build a 17-point lead, Tatum managed just four points in the second half on 2-of-6 shooting with five turnovers. Notably, he missed mid-range attempts on back-to-back possessions in the final two minutes. The first could have pushed the Celtics' lead back up to three, while the latter would have put them in front.

    According to recent reports, "The four turnovers I had in the third quarter really put us out of sync," Tatum remarked. "In those situations, I gotta communicate better, I gotta execute better, I gotta take care of the ball. I think that kinda put us in a hole, and was the turning point for the game.".

    This defeat was the first time all season that the Celtics have lost back-to-back games. Now 11-4, the Celtics are 1 ½ games back of the Philadelphia 76ers for the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference. Come April, when seeding battles are heating up, the Celtics may rue this one.

    It has been revealed that in the second half, as their lead melted away, the Celtics turned the ball over 11 times, were called for 20 fouls (which led to 22 Nuggets free throws) and shot 2 of 19 from 3-point range. Two of the Celtics' four defeats this season have now involved a major blown lead: 22 points against the Detroit Pistons on opening day and 17 points against the Nuggets.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • After winning just one of its first nine games during the 2025 season, the Newly introduced Orleans Saints were able to gain momentum during the second half by winning five of their last eight with newly installed rookie quarterback Tyler Shough.
    • Sources indicate that one of those decisions was selecting Arizona State wide receiver Jordyn Tyson at No.
    • According to recent reports, tyson emerged from the pre-draft process as WR1 on my personal board, but his unavailability impacted his stock.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After winning just one of its first nine games during the 2025 season, the Newly introduced Orleans Saints were able to gain momentum during the second half by winning five of their last eight with newly installed rookie quarterback Tyler Shough. New Orleans carried that positive spirit into the offseason and made personnel moves in support of the young quarterback.

    Sources indicate that one of those decisions was selecting Arizona State wide receiver Jordyn Tyson at No. 8 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft.

    According to recent reports, tyson emerged from the pre-draft process as WR1 on my personal board, but his unavailability impacted his stock. He missed 20 games, including the entire 2023 season, over four seasons in college. When available, Tyson, who began his collegiate career at Colorado, was one of the most productive receivers in college football. He amassed 158 receptions for 2,282 yards and 22 touchdowns in just three seasons.

    In a recent development, discussions involving Tyson and Ohio State's Carnell Tate, who was taken No. 4 overall, often referred to Tate as the bigger receiver and Tyson as the more explosive option. But this failed to acknowledge that Tyson was similar in size to Tate.

    In a recent development, the sample size is small, but Tyson has been impactful in two games played. He has been targeted on 38.3% of routes run for 120 yards. His usage has been a near-even split between the slot and the boundary.

    Tyson comes from an athletic family — he's the brother of Cleveland Cavaliers guard Jaylon Tyson — and it's noticeable. Jordyn is explosive in and out of his breaks. He will run through arm tackles after the catch and has the range to go high or low. His route-running has been inconsistent, but he does not tip his breaks. Tyson will attack the ball in the air, but he did have a fumble in the Browns game.

    Jordyn Tyson first down ➡️📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/8PnWK6dh4K.

    Upcoming Orleans was reportedly interested in LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane before Kansas City traded up. Miami edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. was another player commonly linked to the NFC franchise. Bain has been underwhelming thus far.

    Tyson's production will not compare to the Browns' Denzel Boston or K.C. Concepcion, or even Tate. He missed too many games so far this season, but Tyson belongs in the conversation from a sheer talent perspective. He is a fluid athlete with a legitimate ability to evade would-be tacklers.

    Injuries are difficult, if not impossible, to predict, so projecting Tyson's career would be reckless. Availability will always be the hot topic regarding Tyson, but on-field performance has justified the Saints' belief in him as a top-10 overall talent.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Vanessa Bryant, the widow of Los Angeles Lakers legend Kobe Bryant, has denied a report that she is teaming up with two-time Lakers champion Pau Gasol to attempt to purchase the Los Angeles Sparks.
    • "Another rumor out today… I have never had any conversations about being an NBA or WNBA owner.
    • In a recent development, sports Business Journal reported on Wednesday that Bryant and Gasol were interested in the Sparks, which were put up for sale in October.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Vanessa Bryant, the widow of Los Angeles Lakers legend Kobe Bryant, has denied a report that she is teaming up with two-time Lakers champion Pau Gasol to attempt to purchase the Los Angeles Sparks.

    "Another rumor out today… I have never had any conversations about being an NBA or WNBA owner. If that was true I would announce it. I'm just over here undecided on what seasonal coffee flavor I like and over caffeinated," Bryant wrote on Instagram. "I can only speak for myself. I don't know what anyone else does or does not have going on.".

    In a recent development, sports Business Journal reported on Wednesday that Bryant and Gasol were interested in the Sparks, which were put up for sale in October. Owner Mark Walter, who has been shedding assets amid an FBI and SEC investigation into his wealth management firm, is seeking a record-shattering $700 million for the franchise and its yet-unopened practice facility, according to Bloomberg. The current record for a WNBA team sale is $300 million, which Tilman Fertitta paid for the Connecticut Sun before moving the franchise to Houston to revive the Comets.

    Notably, Josh Kushner and Bob Iger, who purchased the Lakers from Walter earlier this year, are reportedly uninterested in the Sparks. Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer reportedly considered bidding on the team in 2024, but is right now prohibited for submitting a bid because he is serving a one-year suspension from the NBA over his role in the Aspiration scandal. However, at least one of the groups bidding for the Sparks, a group of investors put together by Swish Partners, would consider moving the team to Ballmer's Intuit Dome.

    It has been revealed that gasol already has a financial stake in the WNBA, as he invested in the league's 2022 capital raise. Bryant frequently attends Sparks games and has brought WNBA players in to host clinics at the Mamba & Mambacita Sports Foundation. The late Kobe Bryant was a prominent figure in the women's basketball community, especially coaching his late daughter Gianna's AAU team. Gianna hoped to play for the University of Connecticut and presumably the WNBA afterward before tragically dying in the helicopter accident that killed her father and seven others in 2020.

    Sources indicate that several former NBA players own or have owned minority stakes in WNBA teams, including Magic Johnson (Sparks), Dwyane Wade (Chicago Sky), Kyle Lowry (Toronto Tempo) and Grant Hill and Chris Webber (the upcoming Detroit expansion team set to begin play in 2029). However, no former NBA player holds the governorship of a WNBA team. Gasol could change that. If we expand to immediate family, Bryant could become the first spouse of a former NBA player to hold a controlling interest in a WNBA team, though at this stage, the exact structure of a possible Bryant-Gasol bid and the other investors who could be involved are not clear.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the hot stove is starting to heat up.
    • We're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up.
    • According to recent reports, the Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team announced on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the hot stove is starting to heat up. On Tuesday, David Bednar and Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer while Randy Arozarena, Brandon Lowe, Adrian Morejon, Trevor Rogers, and Seiya Suzuki declined it. Those five are now attached to draft pick compensation. Also, the White Sox landed righty Dustin May on a three-year contract.

    We're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the key offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Wednesday's hot stove happenings.

    According to recent reports, the Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team announced on Wednesday. Fortes will take over as Adley Rutschman's backup catcher. He is projected to make $3.4 million or so through arbitration in 2027, which is a pricey sum for a backup catcher, particularly for a small payroll team like the Rays. Connor Wong has been designated for assignment by the Red Sox in a corresponding move.

    Fortes, 30, had a career-best season at the plate in 2026, though his defensive numbers took a major dip. The Rays acquired Liam Hicks at the trade deadline and he is their clear-cut starting catcher. Kenny Piper, who made his MLB debut in August, could step in as the backup until top prospect Caden Bodine is ready, which could be as soon as next summer.

    In a recent development, the Blue Jays and Dodgers had in-person meetings with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Tuesday, reports ESPN. He will meet with the Padres later this week and already met with the Mets on Monday. Rival executives expect it to come down to Blue Jays and Mets, per ESPN. Toronto has a history of pursuing top free agents but missing out (Shohei Ohtani, Kyle Tucker, etc.).

    Skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Scott Boras clients. The Dodgers are remarked to have interest in a short-term contract with a large annual salary, something that is unlikely to appeal to Skubal. He's poised to land a record contract for a pitcher, perhaps even more than $400 million.

    Sources indicate that star shortstop Corey Seager has expressed an openness to a trade to only a "handful of teams," reports ESPN. Seager has a full no-trade clause and can pick his destination, and was reportedly quite picky as a free agent five years ago. The Rangers are open to trading Seager, as well as Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi, who also have full no-trade protection. deGrom already reportedly invoked his no-trade clause at last season's deadline to spike a deal to the Braves.

    It has been revealed that seager, 33 in April, had surgery to remove a bone spur from his elbow last month, and was limited to 102 games by injuries in 2026. When healthy, he has typically beibeeng very good, but the injuries and surgeries are mounting. Seager is owed $31 million annually through 2031. Texas would likely have to eat some money to facilitate a trade.

    In a recent development, on Tuesday, the Padres hosted free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki for a recruiting visit, according to ESPN. San Diego aggressively pursued Suzuki when he initially came over from Japan five years ago, but he opted to sign with the Cubs instead. We ranked Suzuki as the seventh-best free agent available this offseason, and the third-best free agent position player.

    In a recent development, san Diego needs rotation help more than anything this offseason, though they could use another middle-of-the-lineup bat as well. They could sign Suzuki, plant him in right field, and move Fernando Tatis Jr. back to the infield, where he played 53 games at second base this past season. It was Tatis' first action on the infield since he was the team's starting shortstop in 2021.

    Industry observers note that after signing Jake Bauers, president of baseball operations Craig Breslow said it is "hard to envision that there's something significant on the horizon" for the Red Sox, according to the Boston Globe. That doesn't mean the Red Sox won't do something significant later in the offseason, perhaps after the lockout, but, right now, there is nothing major in the works.

    Breslow's next order of business is unclogging his outfield/DH logjam, which could involve trading or even non-tendering Jarren Duran. The Red Sox also have four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, John Oviedo) and could trade from that depth. Otherwise, Boston has no glaring roster challenges remaining this offseason.

    Industry observers note that free agent slugger Randy Arozarena is seeking well over $100 million and could end up waiting until after the lockout to sign, according to ESPN. For now, teams are balking at that asking price, but that isn't unusual this early in the offseason. The Orioles and Yankees are among the clubs reported to have interest in Arozarena, our ninth-ranked free agent.

    Although Arozarena had the better 2026 season, Suzuki is considered the more desirable free agent because he's a much better defender. They're roughly the same age and are comparable hitters, but Arozarena is a borderline DH at this point. Right-handed power is in shockingly short supply, though. He (and Suzuki) would improve almost any lineup. As noted above, both players declined the qualifying offer from their respective teams, which means they are tagged with draft pick compensation.

    The Phillies are receiving trade calls about righty reliever Orion Kerkering, reports The Athletic. Kerkering struggled badly in the second half, allowing 25 runs and 43 baserunners in his final 19 ⅓ MLB innings of the season. The Phillies optioned him to Triple-A a week before the end of the regular season and did not carry him on their Wild Card Series roster.

    Still only 25, Kerkering has a history of missing bats at a high level and experience in late-inning situations. He will remain under team control through 2029. The Phillies certainly don't have to trade him. They could keep him and even send him to Triple-A next season. It never hurts to listen, however, and other teams presumably see Kerkering as a buy-low candidate.

    Veteran righty Frankie Montas hit 98 mph and wowed scouts during a workout in Arizona this week, reports The Athletic. Multiple general managers were in attendance, and it's possible Montas will land a guaranteed major-league contract. He is rehabbing from Tommy John surgery and has not pitched in an MLB game since August 2025.

    According to recent reports, pitching is always in demand, especially cheap pitching with upside behind league-average innings. Montas, 34 in March, has not been healthy and effective at the same time since 2022, though he looked good during his showcase and he has a reputation for being an excellent teammate who mentors young pitchers. That will only help his case.

    Indianapolis Colts (3-8) is finally pulling the plug on its struggling quarterback. The Colts are releasing Daniel Jones, the team revealed on Friday, just months after Jones re-signed with the Colts on a two-year, $88 million contract with $49.49 million fully guaranteed this past offseason. According to CBS Sports' ex-NFL agent Joel Corry, the Colts will carry a $35.2 million dead cap hit in 2027 from his $44 million signing bonus that was prorated through 2023 with three void years attached to his contract. The team saved $11.6 million in 2027 by releasing him now, since Jones was scheduled to have a $46.8 million salary cap hit next year. The Colts don't have a first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft since they traded both their 2026 and 2027 first-round picks to the New York Jets for cornerback Sauce Gardner at the 2025 NFL trade deadline.

    In a recent development, indianapolis' 26-3 faceplant on Thursday Night Football against the Houston Texans marked Jones' sixth straight game with an interception, the longest streak by a Colts player since Curtis Painter was filling in for an injured Peyton Manning in 2011. Per CBS Sports Research, that also made him the first quarterback since Jim Hart in 1979 to start each of his first 11 games of a season and have no games with more passing touchdowns than interceptions. Jones leads the league in turnovers (16), including a career-high 13 interceptions. His 65.4 passer rating is also the worst in the NFL this season.

    Expected points added (EPA) per dropback.

    * Out of 31 qualified quarterbacks.

    Jones has earned $166.9 million over his eight-year NFL career strictly from his player contracts. He did so by peaking just in time to get paid, with decent play in the final year of his rookie deal with the Latest York Giants and his one-year deal with the Colts. With 2026 not being a contract year for Jones, his play has plummeted in his first year back from suffering a torn Achilles that cut short his 2025 campaign.

    Recent findings suggest that per Shane Steichen, we have released QB Daniel Jones. pic.twitter.com/jdGAZqj9ZI.

    In a corresponding move, the Colts named 2023 fourth overall pick Anthony Richardson their starting quarterback going forward. He requested a trade this past offseason after Indianapolis prioritized Jones over his own development. Richardson attempted just two passes in 2025 after suffering a freak eye injury in the pregame of Week 6.

    In a recent development, when Richardson was last the Colts' starter in 2024, he led the NFL in yards per completion (14.4) while ranking dead last in completion percentage (47.7%). That made him the first player to accomplish the feat since Heath Shuler in 1994 and just the fourth player to do so since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger.

    Sources indicate that per Shane Steichen, Anthony Richardson Sr. will be the starting quarterback. pic.twitter.com/V4JOYzO7SU.

    It has been revealed that this was a move the Colts had to make because the defense refused to take Jones' arm seriously, which has severely hampered three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor's production. This season, Indianapolis has faced the eighth-lowest rate of light boxes in the league on run plays, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. With Taylor rushing for 21 yards on 11 carries in Week 11, he now has 18 consecutive games without 100-plus rushing yards, the longest drought of his seven-year career. Richardson and his rocket-launcher right arm, which led the NFL in yards per completion (14.4) in 2024, should at least give opposing defenses pause as they consider whether to crowd the line of scrimmage to keep Taylor down.

    According to recent reports, so where could Jones land next? There are three teams who are uniquely positioned to be in line for Jones' services for the remainder of the 2026 season. Let's take a look at those three teams below.

    Sources indicate that with a 5-5 record, the defending AFC champion Upcoming England Patriots are just one game back of the conference's seventh and final playoff spot currently occupied by the 6-4 Cleveland Browns. Despite consecutive blowout losses against the Green Bay Packers (45-27) and the Detroit Lions (35-10), they are still right in the mix to reach the 2026 postseason. However, face-of-the-franchise quarterback Drake Maye went down in Week 10 against the Lions with what is reportedly a fractured fibula. That injury might sideline him for the rest of the season.

    If New England decides it doesn't want to roll with undrafted veteran Tommy DeVito at quarterback, Jones could be a fit with the Patriots. DeVito has just eight NFL career starts while Jones has 93. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels could see Jones as a scheme fit after he had another former Patriots assistant, Brian Daboll, as his New York Giants head coach for three seasons.

    The Baltimore Ravens are in a similar spot as the Patriots. With a 4-6 record in 2026, they are still in the hunt for the AFC's No. 7 seed, and they're also without their starting quarterback. Two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson is on injured reserve after having surgery for a broken and dislocated right thumb on his throwing hand. The Ravens traded for veteran journeyman Jacoby Brissett, but he doesn't appear to be the answer. Brissett was the only quarterback who couldn't light up the struggling Dallas Cowboys or win against the Los Angeles Chargers this season. He was rough (340 yards passing and an interception on 33-of-49 through the air) in a 23-20 Monday Night Football home defeat against LA, giving the Chargers their first win of the season to close out Week 10. It's no surprise he has the lowest rate of explosive passes per dropback in the league (5%), per CBS Sports Research.

    Putting Jones out there instead would give the Ravens a quarterback who is four years younger than the 33-year-old Brissett, who is more willing to push the ball downfield.

    The Philadelphia Eagles are now 2-7 and on a seven-game losing streak because of their injury-plagued offense. Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots, while wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) have also dealt with nagging injuries this year. Barkley and Smith have been on the field for just 14% of the Eagles' offensive plays in 2026, down from 54% in 2024 and 67% in 2025.

    If the Eagles prefer Jones's 93 career starts of experience over 2023 sixth-round pick Tanner McKee (5 career starts) and 2024 sixth-round pick Joe Milton (1 career start), he could make sense in Philadelphia.

    #107678. Ranking the NBA's most hopeless teams: Which franchise is in the bleakest situation? And who can't fix it?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2141 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Ranking the NBA's most hopeless teams: Which franchise is in the bleakest situation? And who can't fix it?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2141 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Milwaukee Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo as an opponent for the first time on Wednesday, and it didn't go well.
    • Milwaukee knew it would spend this season in the cellar.
    • Industry observers note that to be clear here, we are operating in terms of championship equity.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Milwaukee Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo as an opponent for the first time on Wednesday, and it didn't go well. Though the final score highlighted only a seven-point margin, the Miami Heat led by 26 after three quarters and were never in much danger. The defeat dropped the Bucks to 1-14 on the season. The greatest player in their franchise's history now wears another jersey, and they're at the beginning of what figures to be a very long rebuild. Things are bleak.

    The question here is how bleak. Milwaukee knew it would spend this season in the cellar. It probably expects to live there for a few years. But how far away from winning seriously are the Bucks really? Are they further from genuine contention than any other team in the NBA? Who, right now, has the bleakest long-term outlook?

    Industry observers note that to be clear here, we are operating in terms of championship equity. We don't care if you have a chance to be a plucky .500 team. No, the barometer we're using here is how likely each team is to reach a conference finals in the next five seasons. We're accounting not only for players on the existing roster, but long-term financial flexibility, available draft assets and the competence of the front office helming these organizations. With all of that in mind, let's rank the NBA's most hopeless long-term outlooks.

    Sources indicate that the broad sentiment following their punishment for circumventing the salary cap with Kawhi Leonard was that the Clippers faced the bleakest future in the entire NBA. That's probably overstating things slightly.

    Remember, we're talking about a Los Angeles team here. Someone, inevitably, is going to want to play for them. All it takes is one player bucking the league-wide trend against superstar free agency and they're back in business. They have an owner who will spare no expense in pursuit of wins, and there's a 26-year-old All-Star in Darius Garland already on the roster. Couple that with the hope generated by No. 5 overall pick Keaton Wagler, and while the path here is extremely narrow, it exists. If the Brooklyn Nets could build a contender without draft picks in the late 2010s, it's theoretically possible for the Clippers to do the same.

    Sources indicate that of course, the Nets weren't subject to that league-wide pivot away from free agency. They didn't have to trade picks to get Kevin Durant or Kyrie Irving in the door. It's much, much harder nowadays to import talent like that without sacrificing picks that the Clippers frankly don't have. The five first-round picks they were docked in the Leonard investigation left them fully Stepien-locked: while they will have (not especially valuable) first-round picks in odd-numbered years moving forward, they can't trade any of them yet.

    In a recent development, there's also the reputational hit the Clippers just took. Will players interested in winning want to risk their careers on a team that cheated? Can the Clippers even appeal to such players given their asset deficit? These are going to be real hurdles. Their path to the conference finals might rely on a star who's not especially competitive. After all, anyone serious about winning could find a team closer to doing so.

    In a recent development, they're a blank slate with one very promising prospect. Darius Acuff is putting up star box-score numbers in his rookie season. That's by no means a guarantee of future stardom, of course. He's as inefficient as you'd expect a rookie to be on this volume. He's taking more shots per game than Jalen Brunson, Tyrese Maxey or Dwyane Wade ever did over a full season. But Acuff has a path to becoming one of the NBA's best offensive point guards. These aren't totally empty calories.

    There's nothing else here. No other notable prospects aside from a handful of likely long-term bench youngsters (Dylan Cardwell, Maxime Raynaud, Emanuel Sharp). Sacramento mostly controls its own picks (aside from the 2031 swap it inexplicably gave San Antonio in the DeMar DeRozan sign-and-trade), but that means less than it used to in the lottery reform era. Its books slowly clean up in the offseasons to come, with Zach LaVine and De'Andre Hunter expiring after this season and Domantas Sabonis and Malik Monk joining them in the summer of 2028, but Sacramento's forays into cap space have typically been unsuccessful. This isn't exactly a desirable destination. That's what happens when you miss the playoffs 19 times in 20 years.

    Sources indicate that that's what separates Sacramento from fellow "one possible star, otherwise blank slate" candidates like the Chicago Bulls. With the hire of Bryson Graham to run basketball operations, the Bulls at least appear to be trending towards becoming a normal organization. Normalcy has eternally eluded Sacramento. The burden of proof is on the Kings. When you've been a mess for 20 years, it's on you to prove that you've cleaned up your act. We'll trust the Kings when they've earned it and not a second sooner.

    For now, they can at least start by actually keeping their success stories in the building. They've kept only one first-round pick this decade through the end of his rookie contract: Keegan Murray, who is now pretty substantially overpaid. Meanwhile, Tyrese Haliburton has blossomed into a superstar in Indiana, while their entire 2021 draft class (Davion Mitchell and Neemias Queta) now starts for Eastern Conference championship hopefuls. They had the unanimous Coach of the Year and the Executive of the Year and fired both within two years. The Kings can't help themselves.

    Sources indicate that there's far more talent in the cupboard here than in Sacramento, but the same organizational concerns apply. The Joe Dumars regime makes mistakes -- the two-year minimum for DeAndre Jordan, not waiting until after the 2025 Finals to trade Indiana its 2026 pick back, everything Shamit Dua has reported about the infamous Derik Queen trade -- that typical teams would never dream of.

    There is not a discernible blueprint here besides, seemingly, "acquire players who can put the ball through the hoop." There are a lot of decent individual creators on this roster. None of them synergize well because so few of them can consistently make 3s and all of them are on-ball players with stylistic clashes. The Pelicans have seemingly made the determination, for instance, that Queen cannot play significant minutes alongside Zion Williamson. That's a reasonable choice... but then why is Williamson still on the team? Or, if the Pelicans view him as a fixture, why make such a risky trade for Queen in the first place?

    The trickle-down effect of putting all of these dribblers on the same team is that none of them seem happy to be on it. Dejounte Murray asked for a trade. Jordan Poole is making googly eyes at the Warriors. Trey Murphy has reportedly signaled a desire to move. What is the proposal here? What kind of team are the Pelicans trying to build? What do they view as their path to genuine winning?

    Sources indicate that that's what distinguishes Fresh Orleans from Sacramento. If the Kings get a few more high draft picks and use them on players that complement Acuff, I'd see the vision. It would require Acuff becoming an All-NBA scorer and those picks hitting, but I see the sort of teams they could build, even if they're unlikely to actually do so. I have no earthly idea what the Pelicans would do with a few high picks because talent is not currently the problem. It's how they're using and nurturing it. It's just hard to envision a team with so little understanding of how to balance skill sets and bring out the best in their players making a serious playoff push. Something significant in the organization would have to change.

    They're the best team on this list in the present, and they've clawed their way back to .500 after a miserable start that included leaks about the team's lack of a point guard. Again, we're dealing in upside here. That's what the Suns lack.

    They control none of their own first-round picks in the seven-year tradable window except for their 2032 selection... which is frozen because they spent the 2024-25 season above the second apron. Even if they had picks, the Suns under Matt Ishbia have never displayed any discipline in using them. Ishbia traded nearly a full draft for Kevin Durant mere days after acquiring the team, spent an unprotected 2031 pick on three far lesser choices that amounted to Mark Williams and a Jusuf Nurkić cap dump, and then spent their 2033 pick as soon as they could access it to get Miles Bridges, whom they've been meaningfully better without thus far this season.

    The most talented players here are all right around their physical peaks. Devin Booker is 30. Dillon Brooks turns 31 this season, and Bridges turns 29. They're going to get worse, not better, and without draft picks, their means of replacing them are minimal. Even the diamonds they've dug out of the rough are on the older side. Collin Gillespie is 27. Jordan Goodwin is 28. The truly young players, like Khaman Maluach and Rasheer Fleming, have thus far underwhelmed. The younger, star-level talent here is Jalen Green, who plays Booker's position and has been a disaster on both ends this season. Why exactly is he still starting over Gillespie? Are the Suns just trying to salvage his trade value?

    It has been revealed that teams like the Clippers, Kings and Pelicans are at least young enough and financially flexible enough to grow. The Suns, at least from an asset and financial standpoint, are essentially all-in on a Play-In-caliber roster. That Play-In-caliber roster is going to get worse as it gets older and more expensive and, without access to top talent in the draft, replenishing it is going to be borderline impossible.

    It has been revealed that the Bucks cherry-pick traits from all of our other selections. The Clippers circumvented the cap; the Bucks are getting investigated for doing so with Gary Trent Jr. The Pelicans have a roster full of overlapping skill sets; the Bucks have a million shooting guards, which made the decision to re-sign Trent for $64 million all the stranger. The Suns don't control any of their own picks and the Bucks won't until 2031 at the earliest. The Kings have the NBA's least-successful owner in Vivek Ranadivé, while the Bucks may have the NFL's in Jimmy Haslam, though he technically won't become governor until 2028 due to Milwaukee's bizarre ownership structure (another point against them, as successful teams tend to have stable leadership rather than rotating five-year terms).

    It has been revealed that who is going to be the best player on the team in five years? Brayden Burries is the best long-term prospect, but he profiles as more of a high-end role player. Tyler Herro was an All-Star in the sense that Norman Powell and D'Angelo Russell were All-Stars: they put up major numbers in a weak Eastern Conference. Kel'El Ware was the lottery ticket from the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade and he's been so bad that he's somehow playing less than he did on a Heat team that was trying to win. Without access to their own picks or a market that tends to draw free agents, they're basically hoping someone internal (Nate Ament? Ryan Rollins?) breaks out or that they hit on a pick far later than you should rely on.

    Industry observers note that you could argue that just by virtue of being in the Eastern Conference, the Bucks have a cleaner path to the final four than those West teams do because they don't have to worry about Victor Wembanyama or the specter of healthier versions of the Oklahoma City Thunder down the line. That's fair, but as we've seen this year, injuries loom over every season. You know what else the West has aside from those two juggernauts? The four other teams on this list. The Bucks, by a wide margin, are the most hopeless team in their own conference. They're starting from the absolute bottom.

    Recent findings suggest that this was potentially avoidable. Had they acted sooner and traded Antetokounmpo in 2025 when the whole world knew a deal was eventually coming, they could have secured a stronger return and set themselves up for a quicker turnaround. Alas, the Bucks chose to waive-and-stretch Damian Lillard, locking them into $22.5 million in dead money through the end of the decade so they could sign Myles Turner to a contract that is increasingly looking like $28 million or so per year in... close to dead money. Milwaukee got its championship in 2021, but at this rate, it's going to be a while before it sniffs another one.

    Sonny Gray returns to Twins on two-year, $55 million contract, per report

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (432 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota.
    • Skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray!
    • It has been revealed that gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota. The Twins on Wednesday announced they have signed the veteran right-hander, who spent the 2022-23 seasons with the club. It's a two-year contract worth $55 million with an opt out, reports the New York Post.

    Skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray! pic.twitter.com/Ky2sBhVi57.

    It has been revealed that gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox. He was the AL Cy Young runner-up in 2023, his final season with the Twins. All told, Gray threw 303 ⅔ innings with a 2.90 ERA during his time in Minnesota.

    CBS Sports ranked Gray as the No. 14 free agent available on the market this offseason. Here's our write-up:.

    Gray has reportedly mulled retirement over the last few offseasons, but he intends to pitch in 2027. He's as crafty as ever, using six pitches regularly and giving hitters every look. Hard, soft, sharp break, big movement, etc. Gray's stuff works in such a way that he seems to get a quick first or second pitch out every inning, allowing him to pitch deep into games. He completed six innings 22 times in his 29 starts this past season, which makes him a workhorse by 2026 standards. Gray will pitch the entire 2027 season at age 37 and he's lost enough velocity to shrink his margin of error meaningfully, which creates some over-the-cliff risk. Still, the 14-year veteran is not out of place as the No. 2 starter in a postseason rotation.

    Industry observers note that gray now joins a Twins rotation that includes Taj Bradley, Joe Ryan and Pablo López, who missed last season after undergoing Tommy John surgery in February. Other options include Dean Kremer, Bailey Ober and Mick Abel.

    The Twins are coming off a 2026 season in which they went 77-85 with a -58 run differential. That landed them in third place in the American League Central and seven games out of the third and final wild-card spot in the AL. Although the Twins improved upon their 2025 record, they've now missed the postseason for three straight years, their longest drought in a decade. The Gray addition -- plus catcher Ryan Jeffers' acceptance of the qualifying offer for 2027 -- helps the cause, and no doubt the Twins under second-year manager Derek Shelton will be looking to get back to the playoffs in what again figures to be a winnable division.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Arizona Cardinals will use their fourth starting quarterback in four weeks on Sunday, turning to journeyman veteran Josh Johnson against the Kansas City Chiefs.
    • "There is no next step to the playbook; this is going back to the starting table of contents, and that's OK," coach Mike LaFleur said.
    • Joey Aguilar, signed off the Jaguars' practice squad, will be the backup.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Arizona Cardinals will use their fourth starting quarterback in four weeks on Sunday, turning to journeyman veteran Josh Johnson against the Kansas City Chiefs. Carson Beck, the third-round rookie who started last week against the Los Angeles Rams, is dealing with back spasms and was ruled out Saturday.

    "There is no next step to the playbook; this is going back to the starting table of contents, and that's OK," coach Mike LaFleur said. "For a three-and-a-half-hour window, it's my job to figure out, as you know, whatever we can to get the ball moving forward.".

    Joey Aguilar, signed off the Jaguars' practice squad, will be the backup. Aguilar, an undrafted rookie, has yet to see regular-season snaps.

    Arizona has endured a revolving door of quarterbacks this season. The season started with Jacoby Brissett as the starter, but he was benched midway through Week 8. Gardner Minshew took over and led the Cardinals to a win over the Cowboys, claiming the starting role in the process. Brissett was demoted to QB3 and, shortly thereafter, traded to the Baltimore Ravens.

    In his first start, though, Minshew tore his UCL, an injury that required surgery.

    Sources indicate that that led to Beck, the No. 65 overall pick out of Miami, taking the reins. He played just one game before landing on the injury report with a back matter, though.

    Industry observers note that johnson is on his 15th team (including practice squad and offseason stints) in 14 seasons. He joined Arizona after Minshew went down with the injury, and the Cardinals signed him off the Cincinnati Bengals practice squad. The 40-year-old was selected by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the fifth round of the 2008 NFL Draft and has bounced around the league ever since, including time in the UFL, AAF, and XFL. The Cardinals will be the eighth team he has played for in the regular season. He appeared in five games for the Washington Commanders last year, finishing 1-1 in the games he started.

    Johnson will be the second-oldest quarterback to start a game this season, behind 43-year-old Aaron Rodgers.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Brooklyn Nets are no strangers to losing games this season, as they fell to 3-11 on Wednesday night, but in a season filled with lopsided defeats, losing by 30 points to the Chicago Bulls stood out as a new low point.

    According to recent reports, the Bulls also entered Wednesday's game at 3-10 on the season, operating as one of the league's worst teams so far, but Chicago exploded for 137 points against the Nets, with eight players reaching double figures. While Chicago's biggest glitch has come on the defensive end this season, the Bulls haven't exactly been lighting opponents up offensively, sitting 23rd in the league in offensive rating.

    The Nets' complete inability to put up a resistance against the Bulls rang alarm bells in Brooklyn and had veteran Julius Randle calling out his team for an "embarrassing" and "unacceptable" performance.

    According to recent reports, "I've been in the league for 13 years... that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of."Julius Randle didn't hold back after the Nets’ 30-point loss to Bulls. 😳 pic.twitter.com/s3YQ8TxP35.

    Industry observers note that "The main struggle? I don't know, that was embarrassing," Randle said after the game. "Been in the league for 13 years and that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of. And not because of the score. You lose by 30 sometimes -- it's just a bad night -- but it's how we did it. That just, it wasn't cool. Nothing about it was cool. We gotta find a way to figure out the root of it or whatever, but that just is unacceptable.".

    Considering Randle has been on his fair share of bad basketball teams over his career in Los Angeles, Newly introduced Orleans and New York, that's saying something.

    It has been revealed that there are five teams that have separated themselves from the pack at the bottom of the NBA in terms of defense and the Nets are one of them with a 119.0 defensive rating (26th in the league). No one expected much of Brooklyn on that end of the floor with the roster they've assembled, but it's one thing to have lesser talent on the defensive end; it's another to combine that with a general lack of effort.

    This early in the season, the latter is a much larger concern and the Nets have now given up at least 124 points in five of their last six games. If they were able to shrug off some of those lopsided losses to quality teams as life in the NBA, Wednesday was proof that their problems extend far beyond just some schedule losses.

    It has been revealed that giving up 137 to a Bulls team that's been similarly bad this year is, in Randle's words, unacceptable. The concern is that no one in Brooklyn, including Randle, seems quite sure what the exact problem is or how to fix it.

    #107671. NBA's eight biggest disappointments through one month: Injury bug, same old East and an underwhelming champ

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1764 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    NBA's eight biggest disappointments through one month: Injury bug, same old East and an underwhelming champ

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that we're roughly one month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and things are going pretty well in certain respects.
    • Sources indicate that in other areas, things are going … not so well.
    • According to recent reports, there have been so many players impacted by various injuries that it's almost hard to keep track.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that we're roughly one month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and things are going pretty well in certain respects. Luka Dončić and the Lakers are off to a hot start in Los Angeles. Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs have picked up right where they left off after last season's Finals trip. And the Celtics are battling the upcoming-look Sixers at the top of the Eastern Conference.

    Sources indicate that in other areas, things are going … not so well. Below are the eight biggest disappointments so far this season.

    According to recent reports, there have been so many players impacted by various injuries that it's almost hard to keep track. Jalen Duren (hamstring) has missed almost the entire season in Detroit. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are still recovering from knee injuries and have yet to play for Golden State, while Steph Curry is now out with an abdominal tear and Kristaps Porziņģis stepped away from basketball. After sitting out all of last season with an Achilles tear, Tyrese Haliburton is right now dealing with a hamstring concern. Brandon Ingram (Achilles) hasn't made his debut for the Clippers. Austin Reaves is out with a heel injury. Anthony Edwards underwent knee surgery and will miss a chunk of time for the Wolves, and it seems unlikely that Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) will play this season, even though he remains hopeful that he will. Paolo Banchero remains sidelined with an ankle sprain. Ja Morant is out with a hamstring strain. Ben Simmons didn't play a single game for the Kings before tearing his Achilles. Kawhi Leonard (knee) is once again on the shelf in Toronto. And the reeling Jazz are without Jaren Jackson Jr (knee), Lauri Markkanen (hand) and Jusuf Nurkic (toe).

    It's all a huge bummer for the players, their teams and fans of hoops in general. But no team has been hurt more on the injury front than the Thunder.

    It has been revealed that the disappointment here is how unkind fate has been to OKC. The Thunder were close to fully healthy when the season started — and then far from it not long after it began. When OKC beat the Spurs in San Antonio in the season opener — after losing four of five regular season games to them last season, as well as falling to the Spurs in the Western Conference Finals — it felt like a statement that the Thunder were back and we were in for an epic battle between the two teams over who would rule the West.

    Sources indicate that and then all of that was stripped away. Just three games into the season, Jalen Williams — who missed much of last season due to injury — suffered a gruesome fall and had to undergo surgery for a fractured fibula as well as reconstruction of ankle ligaments. In that same fateful game, Cason Wallace tore his labrum and later had shoulder surgery. They haven't been officially ruled out, but if either of them plays basketball again this season, it will be a surprise. Making matters worse, Chet Holmgren tore a tendon in his knee and "underwent a biological treatment" to address it. He'll miss approximately two months, but the Thunder do expect him to return. That's what passes for good news in OKC these days.

    The Thunder are — or were — the deepest team in the NBA. That's a credit to what Sam Presti built. But even OKC has its limits. Losing three of five starters is tough to overcome, even when you're led by the reigning back-to-back MVP in Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. That doesn't mean the Thunder (presently 9-6 and eighth in the West) can't still make a deep playoff run, but the odds of them doing so — and of them fighting the Spurs all season for the top spot — got a lot longer.

    Sources indicate that we were told that this was finally the season that the East returned to its former glory. We were told that the conference would be loaded. We were wrong. (Full disclosure while putting a palm to my face: I might have done some of that telling.).

    Sources indicate that through the first month, the East has been mostly underwhelming. Eight of the 15 teams are below .500. The conference has a combined 17-37 record against the West. Only one of the top seven teams in net rating — the Celtics — plays in the East. Five of the top six teams by point differential play in the West.

    The defending champion Knicks are 8-6. The Cavaliers, who made it to last season's Eastern Conference Finals and had championship aspirations of their own, are 8-8. The Magic, Raptors and Pacers — who presently occupy the eight, nine and 10 seeds — all have losing records. By contrast, the worst play-in team in the West right now is Golden State at 8-7. That record would be good enough for the seven seed if they played in the East.

    But maybe we shouldn't be surprised. Since the 1999-2000 season, the West has had the better overall record in all but three campaigns. Maybe next year the East will finally snap out of its funk, but don't bet on it.

    Sources indicate that the Jazz just picked up back-to-back road wins in L.A. over the Lakers and Clippers, but that doesn't begin to dig them out of the deep hole they've made for themselves. The Jazz were gearing up to be competitive in the West this season. So much for that. Like the Thunder, injuries have not been kind to them. Nurkic has yet to play a single game this season, while Markkanen and JJJ have missed significant time with maladies of their own. What looked like a formidable frontcourt has been decimated.

    It has been revealed that still, it's hard to believe how bad the Jazz have been in pretty much every facet. Their first win came in the second game of the season, a one-point squeaker over the Pelicans. It took until mid-November to end an ugly 12-game losing streak and pick up their second and third wins. They're 25th in net rating and point differential. The season has barely begun, and it's already basically wait until next year for the Jazz.

    According to recent reports, the NBA panicked and tried to solve for a problem that wasn't actually an problem, except for a small fragment of people who care more about optics than the product itself. And so the league enacted lottery reform and the latest 3-2-1 system was put in place. This was ostensibly designed to prevent tanking, incentivize winning and bring greater parity to the league. Oops.

    According to recent reports, the Hornets, Wizards, Bulls, Nets and Bucks are all well underwater in the East. The Pelicans and Clippers are drowning in the West, while the Kings and Jazz are even worse. What the league failed to account for is that some of these teams are just organically bad — and now they will have decreased odds at getting better.

    Under the old system, the Grizzlies would be pretty thrilled to see the Jazz struggling since Memphis has Utah's first-round pick in the upcoming draft as part of the JJJ trade. Alas, after making that move, the league changed the rules, which means the Grizzlies can pick no higher than sixth now as a consequence of the newly introduced system preventing a team from picking in the top five in three consecutive drafts. Since the Jazz picked in the top five in each of the last two drafts, that means the Grizzlies are now out of luck with that Utah pick this time around. Womp, womp for them.

    According to recent reports, and on top of it all, fans of bad teams were robbed of the entertaining-in-its-own-way race to the bottom to maximize lottery odds, giving supporters a small silver lining in the otherwise gray clouds of their season. RIP Tank Watch.

    When aren't the Kings disappointing? Aside from their unsightly 1-13 record, the Sacramento front office continues to make baffling decisions. The Kings originally acquired Nique Clifford from the Thunder for a Spurs 2027 first-round pick. Sacramento held onto Clifford for 83 games — choosing to bury him on the bench this season and play him barely six minutes per game — before shipping him back to the Thunder for two second-round picks.

    So the Thunder ended up with the player and a first and the Kings ended up with two seconds.

    One of these organizations is savvy and opportunistic, and the other is the Kings. It's a miracle they nailed the Darius Acuff pick.

    It has been revealed that oof. It has not been a good season to date for Bridges. After going cold to begin their first-round playoff series against the Hawks, Bridges found his form and played well, helping the Knicks go on an epic run that ended with Upcoming York's first championship in 53 years.

    It has been revealed that if that hope was that Bridges would snap out of his early-season funk in similar fashion, the Knicks seem somewhat less patient these days. While head coach Mike Brown has insisted that Bridges is a starter, he has sometimes hedged his bets in crucial situations, going with Landry Shamet or Deuce McBride over Bridges when things get tight and the Knicks need more reliable offense on the floor.

    Through 14 games, Bridges is averaging 7.5 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists on 40.2/28.9/75 shooting splits. It's the lowest scoring output and the worst shooting numbers of his career. As a result, his minutes have dipped to 25.6 per contest. That's also a career low. Bridges is still a plus defender. And he's only 30. The Knicks obviously hope he'll figure it out, as he has in the past. If not, his new four-year, $150 million extension that kicked in this season will start to look worrisome.

    In a recent development, why are we still subjected to … [motions at everything below in the most pejorative fashion possible] ... this?

    ALL 30 TEAM COURTS FOR @EMIRATES NBA CUP 2026 pic.twitter.com/RgBqe1VJCB.

    Why can't whoever came up with the gorgeous GTA VI crossover court in Miami be in charge of the Cup floors instead?

    The Miami Heat are rolling out the “Vice City” hardwood 😮‍💨👏(via @MiamiHEAT) pic.twitter.com/AFcyK2akaV.

    Recent findings suggest that respecting the Cup would be so much easier if they'd give us more of this. Maybe they could dream up some sweet new jerseys while they're at it.

    Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
